You said:
Frequently there is live translation alongside of the speaker. Sometimes the microphone picks up the other speaker from across the room. Is it possible for ChatGPT to filter out the background noise and only pick up the speaker, or is a specific microphone setup necessary?
ChatGPT said:
Great question — this is one of the most important parts of making your translation system work in a real church environment.

Here’s the honest, practical answer:

✅ ChatGPT can handle some background noise… BUT not overlapping voices.
Modern AI speech recognition (including ChatGPT’s audio models) is very good at:

ignoring room noise

ignoring HVAC sounds

ignoring quiet chatter

cleaning up echo

boosting the main voice

However, no AI system today can cleanly separate two human voices speaking on top of each other if they are both clearly audible to the microphone.

So the situation you described — a live translator speaking across the room while the main speaker talks — will cause problems if one microphone picks up both voices.

Therefore:

🔴 If two people are speaking at the same time and their voices reach the same microphone, ChatGPT cannot reliably separate them.
This is true for all speech-to-text systems (Google, Amazon, Zoom, Teams, etc.).

🟢 What will work reliably?
To make your setup work well in a church, you have three realistic options:

OPTION A — Dedicated microphone only for the main speaker
This is the simplest and most effective solution.

Best choices:
A wireless lapel mic (lav mic)

A headset mic

A handheld mic close to the mouth

These isolate the speaker’s voice and dramatically reduce pickup of other voices in the room.

Benefit:
Up to 95–99% accurate transcription

Almost no bleed from translator’s voice

OPTION B — Directional microphone + placement
A directional mic (cardioid or supercardioid) pointed at the speaker helps.

Place it:

CLOSE to the speaker

POINTED AWAY from the translator

Result:
Good isolation unless the translator is directly behind or beside the mic.

OPTION C — Dual-microphone setup
If your church already uses live translators (e.g., Spanish-speaking translator), then:

The pastor uses one mic → fed into the web app

The translator uses a separate mic → NOT fed into the app

This ensures the app only hears the primary speaker.

❌ What will not work well
Using a laptop microphone in the middle of the room

Using a phone mic on a pew

Using a microphone that picks up the whole sanctuary

Using one mic to capture both speaker and translator at the same time

These cause overlapping speech problems.

🧠 But… can the app be trained to prefer ONE voice?
Yes!

We can add features like:

✔️ Voice activity detection
It detects the person closest to the microphone.

✔️ Noise suppression
Removes background hums, fans, noise, reverb.

✔️ Language filtering
If the translator speaks in Spanish but the speaker is in English, we can prioritize English input.

But none of these can fully separate two clear human voices speaking together.

⭐ RECOMMENDED SETUP FOR A CHURCH
Ideal simple setup for you:

1. Pastor or worship leader wears a lapel or headset mic
This audio goes into your phone/tablet/computer running the web app.

2. Translator speaks into a different mic but is NOT fed into the app
Congregants choosing Spanish/Serbian/Italian/etc will read translations from the app, not from the human translator.

3. The app handles translation into all languages
This makes the human translator unnecessary (optional backup only).

the app settings to reduce background noise

Good — yes, you do need a decent microphone to make the system work well. But “decent” doesn’t necessarily mean very expensive: depending on your setup, you have several good options.

Here’s a breakdown of what to think about, plus recommended mics + how to plug one into your web app system.

🎤 What Kind of Microphone You Need
Why a mic matters

So your app hears the main speaker clearly.

Prevents translation voice or room noise from muddying up the input.

Reduces background noise so transcription + translation are more accurate.

Mic Types to Consider

Lavalier (Lapel) Microphone

Clips to the speaker’s shirt.

Very close to the mouth → clean input.

Headset Mic

Worn on the head. Great isolation, very stable pickup.

Directional / Cardioid Microphone

Picks up sound from one direction. Good if mic is on a stand pointing at the speaker.

USB vs Analog

USB mic: Plug directly into a phone/laptop running your web app. Very easy.

XLR / analog mic: Higher quality, but you’ll need an audio interface (more cost & complexity).

Noise Handling

A good mic + correct placement helps a lot.

Some mics have noise reduction or built-in circuits to reject background.

But microphone choice matters more than AI cleaning up voice overlap — you want the mic to isolate your speaker as much as possible.

🧱 How to Hook It Into Your Web App
Connect the mic to your device

If it’s a USB mic → plug it into the computer / tablet / phone running the web app.

If it's an analog mic (3.5mm jack) → plug into the headphone/mic jack of your device (or use an adapter).

Set input source in the browser

In your web app, when capturing microphone with getUserMedia, make sure you select the correct audio input device.

For example, navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ audio: { deviceId: yourMicDeviceId } })

Test and adjust gain

Do a test run: speak in normal voice, check audio levels.

Make sure it doesn’t clip (too loud) but is also not too quiet.

Place the mic properly

For lav mics: clip near chest / collar, not too close to the mouth but also not too far.

For directional mic: angle it well toward the speaker.

Noise suppression in app (optional)

You can run simple noise suppression / filtering on the client before sending to ChatGPT, but primary isolation should come from mic + placement.

📱 How vibration behaves with phone settings

This feature uses Vibrate API, not sound →
it never makes noise, even if the user’s volume is up.

Only vibration is triggered.

Phone's global vibration settings

Mobile browser security rules

Translation System Spec

Translation System Specification (Clean Consolidated Version 1.0)
Note: This is the first fully consolidated and polished specification based on all decisions finalized so far. All rules are global, unified, and simplified for maximum reliability and ease of use.

1. System Overview
The system provides real-time multilingual transcription and translation for live teaching, preaching, counseling, and other spoken sessions. It supports multiple rooms, multiple simultaneous sessions, and multiple admins, while maintaining a simple, consistent experience for users.

2. Rooms
Each room has one unique URL and QR code.

Users enter a room’s session using the public room URL or QR code.

Admins access all rooms through a private admin URL.

Rooms can be added, renamed, enabled, or disabled in the admin panel.

Users’ language preferences carry across all rooms.

3. Sessions
A room may host multiple sessions over time, but only one active session at a time.

A session consists of:

Live transcription

Live translation

Optional original-language text view (advanced)

A concluding banner

A three-minute post-session transcript availability window

4. Admin Roles and Control
All admins are equal.

No super-admin roles exist.

At any moment, exactly one admin has session control for a given room.

4.1 Controlling Admin Rights
The controlling admin is the only one who can:

Start the session

Stop the session

Pause the session

Resume the session

Restart after session end

4.2 Non-Controlling Admin Rights
Non-controlling admins may:

Change settings that do not directly change session control

Adjust room parameters, including translation preferences and banner text

Adjust audio features and accessibility settings

Manage Bible version mappings

Request control

Non-controlling admins may not:

Start, stop, pause, or resume the session

5. Unified Control Transfer Model
The following rules apply universally whenever control might change:

5.1 Control Requests
When a non-controlling admin requests control:

A 15-second countdown begins (admin-adjustable)

The controlling admin may deny the request

If not denied before the timer expires → control transfers automatically

5.2 Disconnects / App Background / Browser Tab Inactive
If the controlling admin disconnects or the tab goes inactive:

A 15-second reconnection window begins (same global timer)

If the admin returns → control remains

If not → control passes automatically to another available admin

If no other admin exists → the session continues without a controller

5.3 Global Inactivity End Timer
If the controlling admin never returns and no other admins are present:

The session automatically ends after the Global Inactivity Period (default: 3 hours)

This duration is admin-adjustable

All transfer and inactivity mechanisms use the same unified timing system.

6. Admin Interface
Two views exist:

6.1 Simple View
For speakers or anyone needing quick access:

Large buttons for Start / Stop / Pause / Resume / Restart

Session status indicator

Button to enter Full View (gear icon)

6.2 Full View
Comprehensive controls and configuration

Button to return to Simple View

Ability to:

Manage settings

Edit concluding banner text

Manage Bible version mapping

View and manage rooms

Adjust audio and accessibility settings

Review session logs and performance stats

7. User Interface
7.1 First-Time User Setup
Center-screen language selector

"Other languages" option

Admin-customizable text

Default minimal appearance unless admin chooses a banner or additional text

7.2 During the Session
Users only see:

The transcript in their selected language

Optional original language if they enable advanced mode

Users can change languages at any time

Transcript history updates

Live feed continues seamlessly

7.3 Paused Session
Displays customizable message: "Translation paused…"

Automatically resumes when the controlling admin resumes

No user interaction required

7.4 Session End
Transcript remains visible for three minutes

Concluding banner appears at the end of transcript

If user is viewing earlier content, interface auto-scrolls to show the conclusion

Screen clears after three minutes

8. Transcript & Data Handling
Users always receive full transcript (including lines missed during disconnection)

Session transcript is cached client-side

Efficient delta-based stream updates minimize bandwidth usage

Concluding banner is not included in exported transcripts

9. Scripture Reference Linking
Automatically detects Bible references in transcripts

Links them to YouVersion (or future providers) based on:

User language

Admin-set Bible version mapping

Mappings adjustable in admin panel

Works in real time without interrupting transcript flow

10. Accessibility & Disability Options
Available to users in the Settings menu:

Text size adjustments

High-contrast mode

Dyslexia-friendly font option

Optional vibration alerts

Admin options determine which modes are enabled or default.

11. Audio & Auto-Boost
Auto-boost dynamically compensates for soft speech

Admin can enable/disable or adjust it

System respects device volume and vibration settings

12. Multiple Rooms & Horizontal Scalability
Admin panel supports creation of additional rooms

Each room has its own:

URL / QR code

Settings

Bible mappings

Concluding banners

Users never choose rooms manually

Architecture supports future expansion to multiple simultaneous events

13. Future Expansion Capability
The system is designed so that, in the future:

Real-time audio translation (not just text) could be added

Additional translation providers could be integrated

Offline mode could function temporarily during short outages

All current choices preserve compatibility with these future possibilities.

14. Exporting & Saving Sessions
Transcript export available to admins

Export includes:

Original language text

Translated text

Session metadata (date, time, location, scripture text)

Excludes concluding banner

Admin may choose what formats to support (PDF, TXT, etc.) in future versions

15. System-Wide Principles (Global Rules)
Simplicity for users and admins

Only one controller per room at all times

Unified timing system for all timeouts and transfers

No cluttered controls or overly granular settings

Smooth, uninterrupted user experience

Admin operations fully transparent to users

End of Specification v1.0
This document will continue to be updated as additional features and refinements are finalized.

This would mean:

The original transcript is the only “pure” record.

Each language file is a “full translation,” not a partial capture.

Pros: Extremely consistent.
Cons: The per-language files are translations, not reflections of actual spoken language.

The original transcript splits by spoken language (Option A).

The translated transcript files contain the full session in the user’s selected translation language.

This creates:

Original transcript → accurate language-by-language breakdown

Translated transcripts → complete unified translations, one per translation language

Pros: Both accurate AND user-friendly.
Cons: Slightly more complex.

✅ RECOMMENDED SOLUTION FOR ISSUE 1 — Audio Input Chain
1. How the system identifies usable microphones
Recommendation
Only devices explicitly listed in the Room’s Microphone Priority List will ever be tested.

Meaning:

The system does not check every admin’s device.

It only checks the devices in the list, in the order defined by the admin panel.

If an admin adds a device to the list, then and only then does the system attempt to confirm microphone access.

Why
Prevents browser permission chaos

Avoids dozens of devices asking for microphone access

Clear and predictable behavior

2. Permission to use admin device microphones
Recommendation
If an admin device appears in the microphone priority list,
the system will request browser/app microphone permission immediately when that admin enters the room.

If permission is denied:

The device is marked “Unavailable”.

It is skipped in the fallback cycle.

Admin is shown a warning in simple language.

Why
Prevents mid-session permission interrupt

Guarantees fallback devices are ready ahead of time

3. If the room’s primary microphone is hardware (line-in, mixer, HDMI)
Recommendation
Hardware/line-in microphones are treated as top-priority, non-interactive devices, and are:

Assumed available unless a technical failure occurs

Given first place in the fallback sequence

Not dependent on admin device hardware or permissions

If such a device becomes invalid:

The system moves to the next priority device

No user disruption

Admin receives a quiet notification banner

Why
Matches real-world church/teaching setups

Avoids unnecessary admin prompts

Keeps audio chain robust

4. Should fallback switching be automatic or require admin approval?
Recommendation
Automatic fallback. No admin interaction required.

Flow:

Mic fails

Auto-retry 5 seconds

If still failing → try next microphone

Quiet banner appears for admins (users never see anything)

System cycles through entire list, twice

Why
Admin is likely speaking and cannot interact

Fastest recovery

Users experience no interruption

Admin still receives helpful notification

5. Admin option to disable fallback?
Recommendation
Yes, but off by default.

Admin panel setting:

Allow Microphone Fallback: ON / OFF

ON (default): full priority cycle

OFF: if primary fails, system stops translation and alerts admins

Why
Some rooms have rigid audio setups (e.g., translator booths, wired mixers) and fallback could be harmful.

📌 FINAL RECOMMENDED AUDIO BEHAVIOR SUMMARY
✔ Only devices in the Room’s Priority List are ever tested
✔ Admin mic permission is requested only if the admin’s device is in the list
✔ Hardware/line-in primary mics are treated as first-class stable devices
✔ Fallback switching is fully automatic
✔ Admins receive quiet banners; users see nothing
✔ Full fallback cycles retry twice
✔ Admin may disable fallback in special cases

6. ADMIN CONTROLS (FULL, DETAILED)
6.1 Admin Authentication
Admins access the admin interface using email + password.

Sessions remain valid for 24 hours of admin inactivity.

Logging in does not affect active translation sessions.

Multiple admins can be logged in at once.

6.2 Simple View vs. Full View
Simple View (Speaker Mode)
Purpose: Maximum simplicity for a speaker who cannot manage complex controls.

Contains only:

Start

Pause

Resume

Stop

Restart (only available when stopped)

Each button must be extremely large and touch-friendly.

A small gear icon opens the Full View.

Full Admin View
Contains everything in Simple View plus:

Room settings

Microphone device check

Language defaults

Transcript controls

Fallback device priority list

Theme settings

Session timing indicators

Access to all rooms (cannot rename a room while active)

A collapse icon returns to Simple View at any time.

7. SESSION CONTROL LOGIC
7.1 Single Admin in Control Rule
Only one admin device controls Start / Stop / Pause / Resume at any given time.

Control Request Process
Any admin may request control.

Current controller has 10 seconds (admin-adjustable) to deny.

If no denial, control transfers automatically.

Controller can explicitly click “Deny Request.”

Completed transfers are logged internally.

7.2 Restart Behavior (Critical Rule)
Restart is only available when session is fully stopped.
This prevents accidental loss of transcript continuity.

7.3 Automatic Session Timeout
Admin Inactivity
After 3 hours of no admin interaction, the session ends.

Adjustable per room.

User Inactivity
Users never “leave” and never “rejoin.”

They simply scroll or stop interacting.

Scroll up pauses auto-scroll.

After 60 seconds of no input, auto-scroll resumes and jumps to Live Updating.

8. AUDIO & MICROPHONE SYSTEM
8.1 Philosophy
The system must be as simple as possible:

Almost all users will plug one single audio feed (from a receiver, mixer, or direct mic) into the device.

Therefore: most rooms need only one microphone input.

8.2 Supported Audio Input Types
Direct phone microphone

External plug-in microphone (TRRS/USB/Lightning/USB-C)

Line-in from a receiver

Line-in from a mixer

Bluetooth is not recommended (latency)

Admins do not have to understand the technical differences — device OS handles it.

8.3 Microphone Priority List
Even though one device is typical, rooms support a priority list:

Example:

Device internal mic

External USB mic

Line-in feed

How admins configure:
Admin sees detected input sources.

Admin drags to reorder.

Top = primary.

Others = fallback.

Fallback logic:
If the microphone connection fails:

System waits 5 seconds for auto-resume.

If still failing, switches to next priority device.

After cycling through all, tries the full list again twice.

If no microphone is usable:

Admins receive an alert.

Users receive no message.

System continues attempting silent recovery in background.

9. TRANSLATION PIPELINE
9.1 Original Input Rule
Everything said by the speaker is captured as:

Original transcript (unedited)
Never altered. Always kept exactly as spoken.

9.2 Translation Behavior
Near-real-time streaming translation.

Output appears line-by-line.

If translation is delayed, user sees nothing unusual.

Errors trigger admin alert only.

9.3 Correcting Translations
Only the room-level default language can be manually corrected.

Optional feature (“Allow Translation Editing” toggle).

No flags, markers, or annotations added.

Corrections replace the translated text in real time.

10. USER INTERFACE RULES

Serif

Dyslexia-friendly

If still no input:

Retry entire fallback chain 2 more times

If still no audio:

Admin alert

Users not notified

Users see no warning

29.2 Admin Roles
There are no special admin hierarchies.
All admins are equal except when one has control of a room’s session.

29.3 Admin Dashboard
Admin enters into:

A list of rooms

Status indicators per room:

Active / inactive

Session running or stopped

Number of users connected

Microphone status

Control is held by which admin (device name)

Selecting a room brings admin into the Simple View, with option to expand to Full View.

30. ADMIN SESSION CONTROL LOGIC
30.1 Control Basics
Only one admin device at a time holds control of:

Start

Stop

Pause

Resume

Restart is available only when the session is fully stopped, to all admins.

30.2 Taking Control
If another admin wants control:

They press “Request Control”

Controller has 10 seconds to DENY

If controller does not deny → control automatically transfers

If controller denies → no transfer

System behavior is consistent across all control transfers

30.3 Losing Control
Control is lost when:

Admin browser tab is closed

Admin device sleeps

Admin leaves the session page

Admin loses connectivity for the global inactivity timeout

Admin explicitly gives up control

Admin session ends (global three-hour inactivity)

If control is lost:

Any admin present may press “Take Control Now”

If multiple admins press at the same time → first-come, first-served

30.4 Auto-End of Session
If no admin returns within the inactivity duration (default 3 hours):

Session auto-stops

Admin notified in dashboard

31. ADMIN UI / UX
31.1 Simple View (Default for Admins)
Contains:

Start / Stop

Pause / Resume

Restart (only when stopped)

Live microphone indicator

Timer of active session

“Request Control” button (if they do not have control)

“Give Up Control” button (if they do)

The goal: Speaker-friendly, no clutter.

31.2 Full View (Advanced Admin Panel)
Contains:

Full session timer

Microphone priority list (read-only during active session)

Top languages list (editable anytime)

Enable/disable translation editing

Transcript download for all languages

Admin list showing who is present

Theme override settings

Error alerts (microphone failure, fallback engaged, translation failure)

Button to return to Simple View

Admin can enter Full View via gear icon.
Admin can exit via "Return to Simple View" button.

32. CONTROLLED ACTIONS AVAILABLE TO NON-CONTROLLING ADMINS
Non-controlling admins cannot ever:

Start

Stop

Pause

Resume

They can:

Download transcripts

Modify settings allowed during live sessions (e.g. top languages)

Enable/disable translation editing

Monitor the session

Request control

View fallback microphone status

Switch to Simple/Full View

Everything requiring exclusive control must be blocked unless the admin has control.

Auto-scroll pauses

Chunk 7 — Translation Architecture, Transcript Logic, Storage System, Editing Rules, User Visibility, Performance Rules
34. TRANSLATION ENGINE ARCHITECTURE
34.1 Input Source
The translation engine always receives one single audio stream per room:

Audio enters through the microphone connected to the controlling admin’s device, OR

Through an attached external audio interface (receiver, mixer, USB audio interface, etc.)

No user device audio is ever used.

34.2 Translation Pipeline
The translation pipeline follows this strict sequence:

Speech-to-text (STT) → Converts live audio into the original transcript

Parsing → Identifies scripture references and detectable formatting

Multi-language translation →

Every active user language is translated in parallel

Translations are cached for all languages used in the session

Output distribution →

Sent to all connected users in their chosen language

Stored locally in user’s device session buffer (up to 1 hour)

Stored in server transcript file for the session

34.3 Translation Quality and Stability
Use consistent translation model for entire session

Translation model selected in the admin panel

Admin can swap models mid-session (rare case), but:

System must reinitialize translation engines

No transcript loss

Estimated 1–3 second lag

Users experience no disruption

35. TRANSCRIPT FILE SYSTEM
35.1 Files Created Per Session
For each session, the server creates:

One original-language transcript file

One file per each language used by any user

Example for 2025-01-04 session “MainRoom”:

20250104_mainroom_original.txt

20250104_mainroom_english.txt

20250104_mainroom_spanish.txt

…etc

35.2 File Naming Rules
File names follow exact structure:

YYYYMMDD_roomname_languagename.ext

Extensions allowed:

.txt

.pdf

.docx (only if explicitly requested)

35.3 Retention Rules
Retention for server-stored transcripts:

Files stored for 60 days

Purged automatically

Deletion cannot be undone

Users never see deleted sessions

35.4 User Transcript Retention
On user device:

Cache lasts 1 hour

Reset if user switches rooms

Reset if session ends

Reset if user clears browser

36. TRANSCRIPT CONTENT RULES
36.1 Transcript Formatting
Transcript always preserves:

Line breaks

Paragraphs (light, structure-based)

Original-order sequencing

Proper sentence separation

Scripture references hyperlinked (unless disabled by admin)

Transcript never includes:

Admin controls

User settings

Session banners in saved files

Saved transcript ends cleanly with:

Last spoken line

No banners, no footnotes

36.2 Transcript Visibility After Session End
User transcript window remains visible for 3 minutes:

Keeps all text

Shows concluding banner at bottom

Does not remove user from app

After 3 minutes → transcript clears automatically

Users remain in the room page

36.3 Transcript After User Returns
If a user:

Leaves the page

Switches to another app

Locks phone

Loses connection

Then returns within 1 hour:

User receives all lines from past hour

Auto-scroll resumes

User session continuity preserved

If returning after >1 hour:

User receives only new lines

No error message

Smooth experience

37. EDITING RULES (ADMIN)
37.1 Editing Permissions
Editing must be:

Explicitly enabled in admin panel

Available only for the default language of the room

Never available for original transcription

Never available for secondary translations

Designed to keep system simple, not a word processor

37.2 Editing Interface
Admins see:

Click-to-edit inline text

Press “Save”

Translations update immediately for all users in that language

Other languages remain unaffected

No flags displayed to users

37.3 Editing Limitations
Admins cannot:

Edit original transcript

Edit scripture reference detection

Edit formatting structure

Insert custom HTML

Re-translate entire transcript at once

Admins can:

Trigger retranslation of a single line

Make small modifications directly

38. USER VISIBILITY RULES
38.1 Users Should Never See:
Admin messages

Microphone errors

Translation engine errors

Control transfers

Admin names

Other user counts

System debug messages

Network failures unless fatal

Users should experience:

Seamless updates

Clean interface

As little complexity as possible

38.2 User Error Handling
If something critical happens (rare):

Users simply stop receiving text

No alert

Live updating section remains blank

When session resumes, text resumes normally

This is intentional for simplicity.

39. PERFORMANCE & BANDWIDTH OPTIMIZATION
39.1 Bandwidth Use
System optimized to:

Send only text, not audio

Send only new lines, diff-based

Cache previously translated lines

Discard old lines after 1 hour on the user device

39.2 Latency Targets
STT should produce text within 0.5–1.5 seconds

Translation should complete within 0.2–0.7 seconds

Delivery to users ~instant

39.3 Server Load Control
Rules:

If 5,000+ users connected to a room → translation batch delivery activates

No reduction in text quality

Small buffering to ensure stability

39.4 Scalability
Rooms require isolated resource pools:

Independent STT

Independent translation engine

Independent transcript store

This prevents one room from impacting another.

46. END-OF-SESSION SYSTEM
46.1 How a Session Ends
A session may end only in one of these ways:

Controlling admin presses STOP

Session times out due to global inactivity timer

Default: 3 hours

Admin adjustable

Session forcibly ends due to admin panel decision

Only the controlling admin can end an active session.

46.2 STOP Behavior
When the admin presses STOP:

The translation engine ceases receiving new audio.

The system generates the final line of transcript.

The system displays a concluding banner to the users:

“The translation has ended.” (admin-customizable)

No concluding banner is saved into the transcript files.

46.3 Automatic Scroll on Session End
If a user is scrolled away from the bottom when STOP occurs:

User is smoothly returned to the end of the transcript

Concluding banner is displayed

No alert or choppy movement

No user interaction required

47. POST-SESSION TRANSCRIPT VISIBILITY
47.1 User Transcript Visibility
After STOP:

Users may continue reading the transcript

Transcript remains available for exactly 3 minutes

After 3 minutes:

Transcript clears automatically

User is returned to a blank screen or logo screen, depending on admin settings

No alerts or messages required

47.2 Admin Transcript Visibility
Admins can:

Access full transcript files (all languages used)

Access them for 60 days

Download TXT or PDF versions

Admins do not see the concluding banner in downloaded files.

48. TRANSCRIPT RETENTION POLICY
48.1 Live Client Retention
Users:

Transcript remains for 3 minutes after session end

Then disappears

Admins:

Transcript retained server-side for 60 days

Configurable but 60 days is default, recommended, and simple

48.2 Server-side Expiration
After 60 days:

Transcripts auto-deleted

No manual admin cleanup needed

Logs of deletion not required (simplicity)

49. TRANSCRIPT FILE GENERATION
49.1 Languages That Receive Files
Separate transcript files are generated for:

Original (spoken) language

Every translation language that any user actively viewed

Files are generated even if only one user had that language open

49.2 When Files Are Generated
Transcript files generate only after:

Session ends

Final transcript is sealed

Concluding banner removed

49.3 File Formats
Two formats generated per language per session:

TXT — simple, universal

PDF — clean, formatted, sans concluding banner

DOCX was considered but intentionally omitted for simplicity and compatibility.

49.4 What Files Contain
Each file contains:

Header:

Date (YYYYMMDD)

Room name

Room ID

Language code

Optional metadata (scripture references, session title, admin-defined notes)

Body:

Full transcript of session

Paragraphs rendered according to translation output

No formatting styles except line breaks

Not included:

Ending banner

UI notes

Hyperlink announcements

Admin messages

System notifications

Each transcript file must follow:

50.2 Consistency Requirements
Room name sanitized (spaces → underscores)

Language code standardized ISO format

Original always saved as “original”

51.3 After 3 Minutes

Users never force session end.

CHUNK 13 — TRANSLATION DELIVERY LAYER (FULL DETAIL)
13.0 Overview
This section defines the complete logic governing how translated text is delivered from the server to users in real time, how text is buffered, displayed, scrolled, reformatted, corrected (in the single permissible correction case), and stored. It unifies all prior rules about transcript behavior, user interface logic, delay handling, queue processing, and user experience expectations.

The core goals:

Simplicity for the user

Users never interact with the system outside of reading translated text and adjusting display options.

No user input fields exist.

No user microphone is ever used.

No user settings can break the flow or require a restart.

Reliability

Messages should appear quickly, cleanly formatted, and without duplication.

Auto-scroll behaves consistently.

Live updates never interrupt manual user browsing.

Universality

Works on all device types, sizes, operating systems, and accessibility configurations.

Respects device-level preferences unless overridden.

13.1 Translation Flow Architecture
13.1.1 Input Origin
All text originates from exactly one audio source at a time.

The audio is always sourced from the device controlling the session (admin device).

This device may be:

A smartphone microphone

An external microphone connected to that smartphone

A laptop with a microphone or mixer input

An audio interface routing mixer output into the machine

No matter the hardware chain, the system treats it as a single audio input.

13.1.2 Speech-to-Text Processing
The system converts audio into verbatim transcript text.

The transcript is not edited, not refined, and not post-processed for style.

No summaries, filtering, or “clean-up” are ever applied.

The transcript must reflect exactly what the speaker said, preserving fidelity.

Pauses, filler words, and natural speech patterns remain intact.

13.1.3 Translation Engine Behavior
Translation is applied only to the transcript, never to audio directly.

Each user-selected language receives:

A fully translated stream

In real time

Using the most recent stable translation engine

Every language is handled independently:

No cross-language dependencies

No shared caches

No shared formatting transformations

13.1.4 Correction Handling
Corrections may be applied only when:

The admin has enabled translation correction for the room AND

The corrected language matches the room’s default translation language

Rules for corrections:

Original transcript is never edited.

Translated text may be edited only in the default language.

Corrections do not have labels or indicators.

Corrections replace prior text for all users currently viewing that translation stream.

A correction is treated as a new message in the stream for saving purposes.

13.2 Message Packaging
Translated lines are packaged into atomic message units.
Each message unit contains:

Message ID

Language code

Text content

Formatting metadata

Timestamp (internal only, never displayed unless Admin enables timestamping)

Room ID

Message IDs
Message IDs guarantee:

Proper ordering

Deduplication

Recovery from temporary device or network interruption

Even though users never see them, IDs ensure system stability.

Timestamps
Timestamps are used for:

Sorting messages

Determining the “last hour” window

Generating transcript files

Resuming sessions

They are not shown to users by default.

13.3 Delivery Methods and Queues
13.3.1 Primary delivery channel
A persistent connection (WebSocket or Event Stream) is used for:

Real-time delivery

Lowest latency

Clean reconnection

13.3.2 Fallback delivery
If the real-time channel fails:

The system automatically falls back to:

Polling every 3 seconds

Error recovery logic

Re-establish WebSocket when stable

Users never see error messages.
Admin sees a small notification if translation service fails.

13.3.3 Queue Structure
Each user session has:

A main message queue

A scroll-lock buffer (when user is not at bottom)

A post-interaction timeout clock (60 seconds)

All queues are extremely lightweight to maintain low-bandwidth requirements.

13.4 Display Logic for Users
13.4.1 Auto-Scroll Behavior
Rules:

Auto-scroll is active whenever user is at the bottom.

If user scrolls up or opens menus:

Auto-scroll pauses immediately

Paused state persists until:

60 seconds of no interaction

User taps “Back to Live”

When auto-scroll resumes:

View snaps directly to live position

No animations or delay

13.4.2 When New Messages Arrive While Paused
They accumulate silently below until:

Timeout triggers OR

User returns to live feed

Users never lose content.

13.4.3 Transition Rules
When no interaction for 60 seconds:

System smoothly returns user to latest message

Auto-scroll reactivates

UI elements fade out if open

13.5 “Last Hour” Session Resumption
When a returning user re-enters a room:

They are treated as a new user unless their cookie persists.

For privacy and simplicity, no login is required.

If cookie is missing or expired:

The system loads the last hour of transcript for that room.

“Last hour” logic uses:

Timestamps

Message IDs

Internal room activity records

User sees:

A fully reconstructed transcript

Immediately updated to the latest line

After 60 seconds of inactivity, system snaps to current live text

13.6 Scripture Hyperlink Behavior
13.6.1 When Hyperlinks Are Generated
Scripture references are automatically detected in transcripts and translated messages.

13.6.2 When User Has YouVersion Installed
Hyperlinks appear

Tap → opens passage in YouVersion app

No modal appears

13.6.3 When User Does NOT Have YouVersion Installed
Hyperlinks still appear, but tapping produces:

A clean modal with:

“YouVersion not installed”

Button linking to app store

“X” to dismiss

Modal disappears automatically after 5 seconds

13.6.4 Admin Option
Admin may toggle:

“Hide scripture hyperlinks” ON/OFF

When off, detecting references is bypassed entirely

When on, full behavior resumes

13.7 Formatting Logic
User may adjust:

Font size (slider)

Line height

Font choice (serif / sans-serif / dyslexia-friendly)

Background and theme:

System defaults to device’s theme

User may override

High contrast option is available

Reduced motion is unnecessary due to minimal animation

Changes:

Apply instantly

Do not disrupt message order

Do not reset scroll position

13.8 Transcript Storage Rules
13.8.1 Storage Duration
Live session data held in active memory for 2 hours after inactivity

Full transcripts stored for 60 days

13.8.2 File Output
For every session:

Original language transcript

Every used translation language transcript

Stored as:

TXT

PDF

13.8.3 Naming Convention
yyyymmdd_room_language.txt
yyyymmdd_room_language.pdf

13.8.4 Exclusions
No banners or session indicators included

Pure text only (except PDF formatting)

No UI elements saved

13.9 Internal Data Consistency Requirements
To ensure accuracy:

No duplicated lines

Deduplication logic is applied only if stable

No merging or summarization

Timestamp order is strictly maintained

Correction events generate distinct entries

13.10 User Simplicity Guarantee
The user experience must obey:

Zero configuration required to begin reading

No warnings, errors, or prompts for microphone, permissions, or login

Only three interactive elements:

Language switcher

Display settings

Return-to-live button (if paused)

Everything else happens automatically.

✅ CHUNK 14 — ADMIN INTERFACE: FULL, EXHAUSTIVE, CONSOLIDATED SPECIFICATION
This section defines everything about the Admin Interface, including authentication, room management, session controls, microphone selection, fallback behavior, admin coordination, events, UI rules, and all decisions made previously in the chat history.

14.0 Admin Interface Overview
The Admin Interface is:

Web-based

Mobile-first but fully functional on tablet and desktop

Designed to be as simple and intuitive as possible

Accessible only through email + password login

The sole location where sessions (start/stop/pause/resume) can be controlled

The location where rooms are created, configured, or archived

Admins have complete authority within the system and are the only users capable of modifying system behavior.

14.1 Admin Login
14.1.1 Authentication Method
Email + password

No multi-factor authentication (MFA) in version 2.1–2.3

Password recovery by email link

Admin sessions persist via secure cookie for 60 days unless logged out

Admin can log out manually

14.1.2 Security Rules
HTTPS required

Passwords stored hashed & salted

Login lockout after 10 failed attempts (15-minute lockout)

Auto-logout after 3 hours of inactivity

14.2 Admin Dashboard (Simple View vs Full View)
14.2.1 Views
Admin can toggle between:

Simple Admin View

Shows active room

Shows session state (live / paused / stopped)

Shows microphone source

Shows start/stop/pause/resume/restart controls

Shows participants (count only)

Does not show timestamps or technical logs

Full Admin View

Shows everything in simple view plus:

Timestamps

Technical connection logs

Room creation/archival controls

Microphone priority list

Translation engine diagnostics

Admin control queue

Active device list

Session inactivity timers

Detailed fallback behavior

Export transcript buttons

Admin can switch views anytime without losing state.

14.3 Room Management
14.3.1 Room Creation
Admin can create rooms with:

Room name

Default language (used for translation correction)

Microphone priority list (optional but recommended)

Admin permissions list

QR code generation (for users to join)

14.3.2 Room Renaming
A room cannot be renamed while a session is live.

Renaming allowed only when session is stopped.

14.3.3 Room Deletion / Archiving
A room may be archived but NOT deleted if any transcript exists.

Archived rooms:

Cannot host a session

Keep transcript access

Are hidden from user homepage

14.4 Admin Control of Sessions
14.4.1 Session States
Only one session per room may exist at a time.
Session can be:

Stopped

Live

Paused

14.4.2 Session Control Buttons
Only one admin device at a time has control over:

Start

Stop

Pause

Resume

Restart (only when session is stopped)

14.4.3 The “Restart” Rule
Restart is allowed only when:

Session is in stopped state

Reset clears temporary caches but does not delete transcripts

14.4.4 Control Ownership
The first admin to interact with controls becomes the “controlling admin device.”

If another admin requests control:

A 10-second timer begins

If current controller does not deny:

Control auto-transfers

If controller denies:

Request is cancelled

If controller is disconnected:

Control transfers instantly to next admin requesting it

14.4.5 Admin Notifications
Controlling admin receives small unobtrusive notices:

“Admin X requests control — 10 seconds”

“Control transferred”

“Control denied”

Users never see admin notices.

14.5 Microphone Source Selection
14.5.1 Simplified Hardware Model
The system treats one device at a time as the audio source.

The device may use:

Built-in microphone

External microphone

Mixer-connected audio interface

Wireless receiver into phone or laptop

The system does NOT attempt to manage audio drivers or hardware; it simply uses the input the device exposes.

14.5.2 Microphone Priority List
Each room may have a microphone device priority list.

A priority list is:

Ordered

Editable

Room-specific

Optional

Default:
The controlling admin’s device is source #1

Admins can create the list:

Example:

Laptop A

Tablet B

Phone C

Alternate Admin Device

14.5.3 Fallback Behavior (Simplified)
Because simplicity is central:

Only one microphone source is expected most of the time

Fallback occurs ONLY between devices, not hardware chains

Fallback Sequence:

Try current device

If audio fails → attempt auto-resume for 5 seconds

If still failing:

Move to next device in room’s priority list

If all fail:

Notify admins (not users)

Keep retrying the entire sequence every 30 seconds

Up to two additional rounds

After final failures:

Show admin alert:
“Audio unavailable. Please check hardware or switch device manually.”

Users always see uninterrupted text (until audio actually stops producing text).

14.6 Admin Settings for Translation
Admins may configure:

Default language for room

Enable/disable translation correction

Enable/disable scripture hyperlinks

Set session inactivity timeout (default 2 hours)

Set control request timeout (default 10 seconds)

Set auto-session-expiration (default 3 hours inactivity)

14.7 Admin Monitoring Tools
14.7.1 Live Monitoring
Admins may view:

Real-time original transcript

Real-time translations

Active users count

Device list

Current microphone device

Error logs (translation failures, audio failures)

14.7.2 Translation Quality Alerts
If translation service fails:

Users are NOT notified

Admins see:
“Translation service interruption — attempting recovery”

System auto-retries silently.

14.7.3 Connectivity Indicators
Admin sees:

Latency

Packet loss

Microphone status

Translation queue status

14.8 Admin Transcript Export
Admins may export transcripts:

File formats:

TXT (plain Unicode UTF-8)

PDF

DOCX (starting version 2.3)

Files included:

Original transcript

One transcript per translation language used in session

Naming convention:

yyyymmdd_room_language.txt
yyyymmdd_room_language.pdf
yyyymmdd_room_language.docx

Banner is explicitly excluded from all saved files.

14.9 Admin Accessibility & UI Controls
Admin interface inherits device theme:

Light

Dark

High contrast

Admin may override theme.

Font controls exist for readability but do not affect user-side fonts.

Reduced motion is not included, as the admin view contains minimal animation.

14.10 Admin User Separation
Users:

Never log in

Never type

Never choose rooms beyond QR code

Never configure audio

Never see errors

Admins:

Log in

Configure rooms

Control sessions

See errors

The separation is absolute.

✅ CHUNK 15 — USER EXPERIENCE (DETAILED, CONSOLIDATED, EXHAUSTIVE)
This section includes ALL USER RULES that have been established, consolidated with no contradictions, and simplified wherever possible without losing detail.

15.0 User Experience Overview
Users:

Never log in

Never register

Never type

Only receive translated text

Interact minimally

Experience a simple, clean, consistent interface

Are always brought into the session instantly

Are automatically rejoined after disconnection

User experience is designed to be:

Ultra-simple

Zero friction

Zero cognitive load

Low bandwidth

Mobile-first

The system should “just work.”

15.1 Entering a Room

Scanning a QR code

Opening a URL directly

There is no homepage, no gateway screen, no login screen.

On first visit to ANY room:

User is asked to choose a display language

Top languages (admin-selected) are shown first

“Other languages…” opens full alphabetical list

Once selected, language is saved in a cookie

Language preference persists for 60 days from last visit

When user enters new rooms, their previously chosen language applies automatically.

15.2 Interface Appearance
15.2.1 Theme

Light

Dark

High contrast

15.3 Text Display

Auto-scrolls as new lines arrive

Scrolls smoothly with minimal animation

Provides continuous translation stream

15.3.2 Full Transcript Access
Users always have the entire transcript available, including:

Everything spoken previously

Everything translated previously

15.4 Scrolling Behavior

15.5 Transcript Behavior

The entire transcript from the last hour
OR

15.5.2 If User Leaves and Comes Back
User gets:

All lines they missed

Returned to live updating section

15.5.3 After Session Ends
Transcript remains visible for 3 minutes.

Transcript ends with admin-selected concluding banner (only displayed, not saved in exported file).

After 3 minutes:

Screen clears to blank

User sees a neutral, empty state

15.6 Scripture Hyperlink Behavior
Hyperlinks appear in translations only if:

Scripture detection is on

Admin allows hyperlinks

If User Has YouVersion Installed

“YouVersion is not installed.”

Link to App Store / Google Play

“X” close button

Message auto-dismisses after 5 seconds

No in-app scripture display

No fallback Bible text

Hyperlinks appear even if user lacks YouVersion—this makes behavior predictable and simplifies user experience.

Sans-serif

Serif

Dyslexia-friendly

Adjust:

Font size (slider)

Line height

Device-default

High contrast

microphone fails

translation service drops

admin disconnects

text delivery temporarily stops

Users simply see a moment of no new text.

15.9 User Session Persistence

Background choice

Advanced mode toggle

Chooses language again

15.10 User Navigation

Cannot upload

15.12 Disability Accessibility

High contrast backgrounds

Dyslexia-friendly font

Adjustable line height

Adjustable fonts

Adjustable size slider

Reduced motion mode is unnecessary because animations are minimal.

15.13 Performance Requirements
User-side performance targets:

Load time < 2 seconds on mobile

Live updates delivered in < 1 second

Zero flicker

Zero UI lag

No heavy graphics

No video

No audio playback

Minimal network usage (<5 KB per sentence)

15.14 Bandwidth Optimization
User receives:

Batch text where possible

Efficient diff-patch updates

Only their chosen language feed

No redundant streams

This keeps the system functional even on very low bandwidth connections.

✅ CHUNK 16 — ADMIN EXPERIENCE (FULL, CONSOLIDATED, EXHAUSTIVE)
This section fully details everything an admin can do, how they access the system, their permissions, their limitations, and the unified system rules.

Everything below incorporates all decisions made so far, including fallback revisions and simplifications.

16.0 Admin Overview
Admins:

Log in using email + password

May operate from phone, tablet, laptop, desktop

Only one admin at a time may control session actions

Non-controlling admins have limited visibility and cannot take actions without requesting control

The UI is divided into:

Simple View (speaker-friendly, minimal)

Full View (full administrative controls)

Can operate multiple rooms but only control one room at a time

Everything is designed to be:

Simple

Low-bandwidth

Reliable

Mobile-first

Resistant to confusion

16.1 Accessing the Admin Panel
Admins access via:

/admin

Login required: email + password

If login is successful:

Admin is taken to the room list

Rooms are displayed with indicators:

Active session

Session idle

Audio status

Last activity

Room creation and room settings are in this same area.

No admin has elevated permanence — no super admins.
All admins share equal privileges except for temporary session control.

16.2 Admin Views
16.2.1 Simple View (Speaker Mode)
This displays:

Start

Stop

Pause

Resume

Restart (available only when session is stopped)

Only the controlling admin may press these buttons.

Other elements:

Current language of original feed

Audio status indicator (simple: green, yellow, red)

Timer showing session duration

Link/icon (gear) to enter Full View

The Simple View is intentionally clean, uncluttered, and prevents errors.

16.2.2 Full View (Advanced Admin Panel)
Contains:

Room list

Room settings

Microphone source selection

Admin-controlled options for:

Default room language

Hyperlinks on/off

Scripture detection

Saved transcript settings

User appearance defaults

Admin activity log

16.3 Session Control Rules (Unified)
Only one admin has control at a time.

Control governs:

Start

Stop

Pause

Resume

Restart

16.3.1 Requesting Control
Any non-controlling admin may tap Request Control.

Then:

Current controller has 10 seconds to deny

If controller does nothing, control transfers automatically

Delay (10s) is admin-adjustable

A denying admin can press Deny to block the transfer.

16.3.2 If the controlling admin disconnects
If they leave the page, or connection is lost, or device sleeps:

Control remains with them indefinitely

Except:

Global inactivity timeout, default 3 hours (admin-adjustable)

After timeout, session ends automatically

Another admin may request control at any time

This prevents interruptions for speakers.

16.4 Session Actions
Start
Begins the session

Activates microphone input

Activates translation

Starts transcript

Only available when session is stopped

Pause
Temporarily halts translation

Users see a paused message (“Translation paused…”)

Auto-resume is off; only manual resume by controlling admin

Resume
Restarts translation

User view returns to normal

Stop
Ends the session completely

Transcript continues to show for 3 minutes to users

Restart
Only available after session is stopped

Clears transcript

Begins a fresh session

Restart cannot be pressed while session is running.

16.5 Microphone Source Rules
System is simplified:

Only one active audio input per room

This may be:

The admin’s device microphone

A device plugged into the admin’s device

A mixer or receiver connected to the admin’s device

Fallback is extremely simplified:

If microphone fails:
System retries auto-resume after 5 seconds

If it fails again:

System switches to next admin device waiting in the room

In order of admin priority list

If all fail:

System retries entire cycle twice

Then notifies admins

Users see nothing unusual

Admins can define device-priority lists per room.

16.6 Admin UI Notifications
Admins (not users) receive notifications for:

Microphone failure

Translation service delays

Connection failures

Someone requesting control

System fallback events

Room inactivity reaching timeout threshold

Notifications must be:

Clear

Non-technical

Mobile-friendly

16.7 Room Management
Admins can:

Create rooms

Rename rooms (not during active sessions)

Delete rooms (not during active sessions)

Set default room language

Set device-priority list

Configure:

Hyperlinks

Scripture detection

Appearance defaults for users

Session timeout durations

Transfer control delay

Access saved transcripts

Download transcripts (TXT or PDF)

16.8 Transcript Management
Admin version retains:

Full original transcript

Full transcript for every language users selected

Timestamps optional (off by default)

Saved using filename format:

YYYYMMDD_ROOM_LANGUAGE.txt
YYYYMMDD_ROOM_LANGUAGE.pdf
Retention: 60 days

Admins may download files anytime.

User-facing transcripts disappear after 3 minutes, but are saved on backend.

16.9 Admin Permissions Summary
All admins are equal except:

Only controlling admin may manage session actions

Any admin may take control (via request system)

Any admin may restart when session is stopped

Any admin may modify room settings

except room name during active session

Any admin may download transcripts

Any admin may adjust microphone priorities

There is no super-admin model.

16.10 Admin Error Handling
Admins see:

Simple warnings

Option to retry microphone

Option to switch microphone

Option to end session

Option to request control

Users see none of this.

16.11 Device Sleep, Disconnect, and Inactivity
Unified rule:

If admin device disconnects → control stays with them

If admin device sleeps → control stays with them

If admin is inactive:

Session continues

After 3 hours (adjustable) → session ends

Users simply see the end-of-session banner followed by blank.

This section fully defines everything a user sees, everything a user can do, and every system behavior involving user interaction.

17.0 User Overview
Users:

Their selected language

Transcript display

Optional advanced view

Optional appearance settings

Language choice

Font preferences

Background preferences

Line height

Font size

View mode

Cookie persistence: 60 days from last visit

If the cookie is lost, they are treated exactly like a new user.

17.1 Initial User Entry Flow

Their preferred language is pre-selected automatically

Their appearance settings (font, size, theme) are restored

If transcript is active:

17.2 Language Selection

17.3 Transcript Display Rules

User Seeing Missed Content

Live Updating resumes immediately

No manual refresh needed, ever

Deduplication handled invisibly

Transcript Visibility Rules
Transcript is visible throughout session

Transcript is not hidden, only overlapped by menus if user opens them

After session ends:

Transcript stays visible for 3 minutes

With concluding banner (admin-defined message)

After 3 minutes: transcript disappears

The concluding banner is never saved into transcript files.

17.4 Handling Hyperlinks (Scripture references)
Users see clickable scripture references if:

Scripture detection is active

Reference is detected during translation

Hyperlink Behavior

Case 2 — User does NOT have YouVersion installed:

“YouVersion is not installed.”

Suggests installing it

Contains button linking to the correct app store

If hyperlinks are disabled by admin
No links appear at all

17.5 User Appearance Controls (Advanced View)

Line height (slider)

Serif

17.9 User Permissions

✅ CHUNK 19 — MICROPHONE / AUDIO INPUT SYSTEM
This part governs how live audio enters the system, how translation is fed, the fallback rules, and how admins manage this.
The philosophy of this system is:

Simplicity first. Reliability second. Everything else third.
Users must never be burdened with audio issues.
Admin interactions must be simple and obvious.
No unnecessary complexity.

19.1 Core Principle: Audio Always Comes From a Device Controlled by an Admin
Only admins can supply audio input.

Users never transmit audio.

The audio source is exactly one device at a time.

The system always uses the Controlling Admin's device unless overridden in settings.

This keeps the system intuitive:

“The admin who has control of Start/Stop is the admin whose microphone is used.”

This is true unless the admin overrides the microphone source manually.

19.2 Primary Microphone Source
The default microphone input is the microphone on the Controlling Admin's device:
This could be:

Device’s built-in microphone

A wired lav or handheld mic

A USB audio interface

An XLR → Lightning / USB-C interface

A wireless receiver plugged into the device

A mixer output connected to the device

Any device audio input recognized by the OS

The system does not care about audio hardware specifics.
Whatever the device sees as its "current mic" is what the system receives.

This matches your priority:

Keep it simple. Use whatever the device already sees as a microphone.

19.3 Room-Level Microphone Priority List
Although simplicity is preferred, you decided:

“Rooms should have a microphone priority list. Top of the list is used first. Fallbacks come after that.”

So for each room:

Admins can create a microphone list:
Example:

Pastor iPhone (priority 1)

Booth Laptop (priority 2)

Backup iPad (priority 3)

This list is:

Room-specific

Adjustable at any time except when session is actively streaming
(avoids transitions mid sentence unless admin intentionally changes it)

19.4 Fallback Logic (After Revision for Simplicity)
You decided:

"I want fallback options, but keep it simple. Usually there will be only one audio source. Fallback can be to another admin device."

Therefore:

Fallback triggers ONLY when:
Primary microphone device fails connection

Primary device loses network for >5 seconds

Primary device crashes or browser closes

Primary device violates inactivity rules

Fallback sequence:
Attempt to reconnect to primary microphone for 5 seconds

Try a 2nd reconnection attempt, another 5 seconds

If still failing:
→ Move to next microphone in the priority list

If list ends:
→ Cycle back to the top
→ Continue retrying until session ends or device recovers

The system NEVER notifies users of microphone failures.
Only admins receive:

Banner / panel alert

Vibration (if enabled)

“Microphone is attempting to auto-recover” message

Users see nothing unusual.

19.5 Manual Microphone Override (Admin Option)
In the full admin view, admins may:

Select a specific admin device as audio input

Override priority list temporarily

Lock microphone to a device for the session

Return to priority list logic

This feature maintains both simplicity and control flexibility.

19.6 How the System Detects Microphone Failure
The system constantly monitors:

Audio packet health

Silence beyond expected threshold

Device heartbeat

Browser focus state

Network connectivity

Microphone is considered failed when:

Audio packets drop for 3+ seconds

Admin device disappears from the websocket mesh

OS signals the audio device was disconnected

Browser tab is closed

Device loses network connection >5 seconds

All of this is silent to users.

Admins see:

A red icon next to microphone name

A fallback attempt countdown

Notification when fallback succeeds or cycles

19.7 Users Never See Microphone Issues
You have repeated this many times, so it is permanently encoded into the spec:

Users NEVER see:
Microphone warnings

Audio errors

“Trying to reconnect”

“Device disconnected”

“Using fallback”

Instead:

The transcript simply pauses until audio resumes

When audio returns, transcript continues normally

Users do not need to tap anything

This is consistent with your vision:

“The system should just work.”

19.8 Audio Quality and Latency Rules
Target latency:

0.5–2.0 seconds average speech recognition delay

Translation delay 1–3 seconds depending on language

Frame processing rules:

Use streaming STT (real-time)

Use chunked translation (phrase-level batching)

No buffering longer than needed

Prioritize speed over strict grammatical perfection

Deduping handles repeated text

Users always see latest phrase appear smoothly

19.9 Audio Source Behavior During Admin Control Transfer
When control switches to another admin:

Audio must switch instantly to the new controlling admin’s device.
Rules:

System automatically switches to new admin's microphone

If new admin has no microphone input:

System falls back to first available microphone in priority list

No interruption for users unless all microphones unavailable

This rule ensures:

Control = microphone power.

Admins can set:

19.11 Non-Controlling Admin Role in Audio System

Take audio control without becoming the controlling admin.

20.0 Purpose of This Section
This chunk defines how the translation engine works, including:

How speech becomes text

How text becomes translation

Timing rules

Quality rules

What users see

What admins control

How fallback and errors work

How transcripts update

How scripture hyperlinks behave

How multiple languages run at once

This section is fully consistent with everything previously decided, including your major principles:

Simplicity, reliability, clarity, minimal user interaction, admin-focused controls, smooth experience, and transcript-based presentation.

20.1 Translation Pipeline Overview
The translation pipeline is:

Audio Input → Real-Time Speech-to-Text (STT) → Phrase Buffer → Translation Engine → Deduplication → Output to Users
Every part of this chain is optimized for:

Low latency

Accurate transcription

Smooth phrase-by-phrase updates

Predictable behavior

No step blocks the others.

20.2 Speech-to-Text (STT)
20.2.1 Type of STT
Real-time streaming STT

Uses chunked processing (sub-second frames)

Produces:

Word-level partial text (never shown)

Phrase-level intermediate output

Finalized segments

20.2.2 Latency Target
0.5–2.0 seconds typical

Hard cap of 3 seconds before flushing partial text

20.2.3 Text Quality Rules
Punctuation is added automatically

Paragraphs auto-inserted based on pauses

Numbers transcribed exactly

Scripture references preserved as spoken

Disfluencies removed if obvious (“um”, “uh”)

Repetitions cleaned (heavy stuttering, repeated words)

BUT:

The original transcript is still considered “as spoken” for session recordkeeping.

Admin editing (only for default language) applies only to translated text, not original.

20.3 Phrase Buffer
The system groups STT output into phrases, not raw text.

Rules:

A phrase is usually a sentence or clause

Phrases are the unit sent to translators

Phrases are appended to transcripts once complete

Users see text appear fluidly, not word-by-word

This eliminates jittery text, improves readability, and supports the auto-scroll rules already agreed.

20.4 Translation Logic
20.4.1 Supported Languages
Every language supported by the translation API, including but not limited to:

English

Italian

Persian (Farsi)

Turkish

Bangla

Urdu

Ukrainian

Polish

Simplified Chinese

And many more

Admin can choose which languages are shown in the “Top Languages” list based on your earlier selection.

20.4.2 How Translation Works
Each finalized phrase is:

Sent to translation engine

Translated into every currently active user language

Deduplicated (see below)

Delivered to users

Added to transcript buffers

If 50 people are watching in 9 different languages, translation occurs for 9 languages.

Users do NOT request translation; the system determines all that automatically.

20.5 Deduplication Logic
You decided:

“If deduplicating can be done reliably, do it.”

Deduping removes repeated STT segments caused by:

Microphone glitches

STT engine repeating uncertain phrases

Temporary fallback microphone overlaps

Algorithm:

Compare last 3 delivered segments with new segment

If >85% identical text: discard duplicate

If slight variation but meaning identical: use better one

20.6 Translation Failures and Recovery
You decided:

“Users should not see any messages except the text itself. Admins should see system warnings.”

So:

Users:
No warnings

No interruption message

Text simply pauses and resumes

Admins:
Full technical error messages

Vibration alerts (if enabled)

Color-coded translation status

Auto-retry logic visible in Full View

Silent in Minimal View unless severe failure

Retry behavior:
Retry every 2 seconds

After 30 seconds → show admin alert (“Translation degraded”)

Continue retrying indefinitely

Never switch languages or fallback models automatically

20.7 Scripture Reference Detection

Support for:
Gen 1:1

John 3:16

Romans 8:28

Ps 23:1

Etc.

“YouVersion is not installed”

X to close

20.8 Translation Display for Users

Auto-resume after 60 seconds of no interaction

Banner behavior:
If paused manually: “Translation paused…” (admin-editable text)

Not included in saved transcript

20.9 Multi-Language Transcript Storage

One file per language

Phrase-level translation

Fast, readable, stable

Admins may select:

20.11 Admin Editing of Translations
Only the default language for the room can be edited

Changes apply instantly to user-facing text

No flags shown

Original text cannot be edited (preserves fidelity)

Optional “retranslate this phrase” button for admins.

20.12 Active Language Set Management
The translation engine loads languages dynamically:

If no one is using French → French translations stop

If a new French user arrives → French translation begins instantly

No admin interaction required

User language selection triggers engine expansion.

20.13 Translation Load Management
If needed to reduce load:

Less-requested languages processed second

High-priority languages always processed first

But every language will be delivered

Latency may vary slightly if load is heavy

(All of this is automatic.)

The system is:

**CHUNK 24 — ADMIN AUTHENTICATION SYSTEM
(Full, Exhaustive, Consolidated Specification)**

This section describes how administrators securely access and operate the system. As always, this adheres to the guiding principle:

Simplicity + Reliability + Zero Friction
Users never log in.
Only admins authenticate.

24.1 Admin Authentication Overview
Administrators authenticate using:

Email address

Password

No phone numbers, usernames, or secondary identifiers.

The system is designed for:

Churches

Events

Conferences

Multisite organizations

Where multiple administrators may need access to the same rooms.

Authentication is:

Simple

Fast

Secure

Mobile-friendly

24.2 Login Process
Step 1 — Admin navigates to the Admin Portal
This is a separate URL:

Example: /admin

Users never see this.

Step 2 — Admin enters email + password
Fields:

Email (case-insensitive)

Password (min 12 characters recommended)

Step 3 — Server validates credentials
Against encrypted stored hashes.

Step 4 — On success
Admin is redirected to the Admin Home / Room List page

Admin is issued:

A secure session cookie

Expiration default: 12 hours (adjustable)

Session auto-renews while active

Step 5 — On failure
Standard message:
“Incorrect email or password.”

No hints

No detail

No user enumeration leaks

24.3 Password Reset Flow
Admins can request a password reset:

Admin enters email

System sends time-limited (15 min) reset link

Admin sets new password

Security rules:

Must differ from last 5 passwords

Must meet strength criteria

Admin accounts cannot be created via this flow.

24.4 Admin Account Management
Admin accounts can only be created by other authorized admins.

This avoids:

Public signup

Unauthorized access

Account sprawl

Each admin is assigned:

Email

Display Name (optional)

Permissions:

Full Admin (default)

Room Admin (optional future expansion)

Active status (true/false)

24.5 Role Philosophy
The system is intentionally flat.

There are no superadmins, per your rule.

Key points:

All admins have equal authority

The only special privilege is session control, and only one admin has control at a time

Control is assigned by arbitration rules, not rank

Admins may hand off control or request it from others at any time

This eliminates unnecessary hierarchy.

24.6 Session Control Arbitration Integration
Authentication interacts with control arbitration in the following ways:

When an authenticated admin enters a room:
They are recognized immediately

They can request control

They can see real-time session state

They cannot interfere with the current controlling admin unless they request control

The system never requires:
Re-authentication during a session

Special permissions

Additional input

Control request works identically in Full and Simple Admin Views.

24.7 Admin Session Timeout
Admin authenticated sessions expire after 12 hours unless:

Admin is in an active session

Admin is actively pressing buttons

Admin is interacting with the admin UI

Expiration behavior:

Admin receives a gentle banner warning 5 minutes prior:
“Session will expire soon. Tap anywhere to extend.”

Any tap or scroll resets the timer

If expired:

Admin is returned to login page

The session in the room continues unaffected

Control is transferred according to your rules:

If admin was controlling and becomes inactive for the timeout period, control is returned as per the system-wide inactivity logic (adjustable)

24.8 Multi-Device Authentication
Admins may be logged in on multiple devices simultaneously.

However:

Control is tied to the device, not the admin account

If Admin A has a phone and a laptop, each can separately request control

Each device is treated as an independent control seat

This allows:

Speaker to operate from phone

Tech team to operate from booth

Redundancy without complex permissions

24.9 Security Requirements
All admin authentication must follow:

HTTPS only

Secure cookies

SameSite=strict

CSRF token matching

Rate limiting (5 attempts/min maximum)

Automatic lockout after repeated failures

Admins notified of suspicious activity

System stores:

Only salted password hashes

Never plaintext passwords

Minimal identifying info

24.10 Admin Logout
Admins can:

Log out manually via button

Allow automatic expiration

Close browser (session cookie persists unless expired)

Users are unaffected regardless of admin logout.

24.11 Summary of Admin Authentication Goals
The authentication system must:

Be extremely simple

Work flawlessly on mobile

Never interrupt live sessions

Never complicate admin workflows

Avoid unnecessary privilege structures

Keep the system secure

CHUNK 25 — ROOM STRUCTURE & ROOM MANAGEMENT
(Full Detail, Exhaustive, Consolidated Specification)

This section defines how rooms function, how they are created, modified, and used throughout the system.
A room = a fully independent translation environment capable of running its own live translation session.

25.1 Core Definition of a Room
A Room is:

A unique translation session location

With its own URL

Its own QR code

Its own transcript storage

Its own admin-configurable settings

Its own default language

Its own microphone/device priority list

Its own live session control state

Rooms allow multiple simultaneous translation events in separate physical or virtual locations.

25.2 Room URL Structure
Each room has:

A unique, permanent URL:

https://domain.com/r/<roomSlug>
A matching QR code

Automatically generated

Stable

Does not expire

Only updates if the admin regenerates it intentionally (rare)

Examples:

/r/sanremo-main

/r/youth-1

/r/counseling-room-3

Slug rules:

Lowercase

Letters, numbers, hyphens

Auto-generated from room name

Can be manually edited during creation (before first save)

25.3 Creating a New Room (Admin Only)
Admins can create a new room via:

Admin Panel → Rooms → “Create Room”

Required fields:

Room Name

Example: Sanremo Main Session

Slug (auto-filled)

Default Language

The language that:

Users see if they have no saved preference

Translation editing applies to

Microphone Priority List

See section 25.7

Optional Room Description

Appears only to admins

Optional Room Notes

For internal organization (not visible to users)

Constraints:

Cannot create two rooms with the same slug

Must have a default language

Must have at least one microphone priority entry

All required fields must be defined

25.4 Room Editing
Admins may edit:

Room Name (only when no session is running for that room)

Default Language

Microphone Priority List

Room Notes

Slug (only when room is inactive)

Admin-Defined Custom Banner Messages

Hyperlink Settings

Color theme defaults

Edits that are NOT allowed during a live session:

Room name

Slug

Deleting the room

Changing microphone priorities

Changing the default language (unless no session is running)

These rules maintain the principle of stability during live translation.

25.5 Room Deletion
A room cannot be deleted if:

A live session is running

Transcript files exist that have not expired (60-day retention window)

Deletion steps:

Admin selects “Delete Room”

System shows a list of transcript files that will be permanently deleted

Admin confirms

Room is removed

URL will show a “This room no longer exists” page

Deleted rooms’ URLs are never reused unless manually done by admins.

25.6 User Experience Per Room
When a user enters a room:

They receive the translation feed for that room only.

Their saved language preference (stored in cookie) is applied.

If no preference exists:

They are shown language selection (top languages + “Other languages…”)

All advanced options & accessibility settings are per-room but stored via cookie so the user retains universal preferences where applicable.

If a user moves to another room:

It is considered a new session

Their language preference carries over globally

Users do not choose rooms — only admins distribute room URLs/QRs.

25.7 Microphone/Input Priority List (Per Room)
Each room defines:

Ordered list of possible audio input devices:
Primary Device / Microphone

Fallback 1

Fallback 2

… etc.

Each device in the list can be:

A specific admin mobile device

A laptop/computer

An attached USB microphone

An audio interface

A BT receiver

Any browser-supported audio source

How the system uses this list:

When the session starts → system uses the top priority device

If audio fails → auto-retry after 5 seconds

If still failing → fallback to next device in list

After exhausting the list → start again at top and retry 2 more cycles

After 3 total cycles:

Notify admins only

Users see nothing unusual

Translation pauses until audio resumes or admin fixes the issue

25.8 Room State
Each room has a persistent state variable:

roomState = {
  sessionActive: true/false,
  controllingAdminDeviceID: <device-token or null>,
  lastActivityTimestamp: <timestamp>,
  sessionStartTime: <timestamp>,
  sessionEndTime: <timestamp or null>,
  adminTimerInactivityExpiration: <configured-time>,
  userTimerInactivityExpiration: <60 min>,
  roomDefaultLanguage: <language-code>,
  microphonePriorityList: [...]
}
This ensures:

Deterministic session control arbitration

Proper session cleanup

Accurate transcript storage

No race conditions

No duplicate control states

No ghost sessions

25.9 Room-Based Transcript Storage
Each room stores:

Translation transcripts for every language that was requested by at least one user

Files are stored per session

Naming format already approved:

25.10 Room-Based QR Codes
