Admin can download QR code for printing

QR regenerates only if:

Admin changes the slug (only possible when idle)

No session state affects QR code.

25.11 Room Ordering in the Admin Panel
Rooms may be displayed:

Alphabetically (default)

By most recently active

By admin-defined manual order (optional)

By building or category (future optional)

Ordering does not affect URLs.

25.12 Room Visibility
All rooms are visible to:

All authenticated admins

No rooms are visible to users except by URL entry

No “room browser” exists for users

If a user attempts to access an inactive room:

They see a blank screen (white)

Then after 2 seconds a small message:
“No active session. Please check your event information.”

No technical detail is shown to the user.

CHUNK 26 — SESSION LIFECYCLE (START, STOP, PAUSE, RESUME, RESTART)
(Full, Exhaustive, Consolidated Specification)

This section defines the precise behavior of a session within a room.
A session = the period during which a room is actively receiving audio and generating translated text.

26.1 Overview of Session Lifecycle
A session has five possible actions:

Start

Pause

Resume

Stop

Restart (only when stopped)

A session can only be active in one room at a time, but multiple rooms can have their own independent sessions simultaneously.

Only one controlling admin device may trigger these actions at any moment.

26.2 Session Start
Conditions Required:
No session is currently active in the room

A controlling admin device exists (first admin to press “Start” becomes controller)

Room has at least one microphone/input source available

Admin must be authenticated

Effects of Start:
sessionActive = true

sessionStartTime = now

Controlling device = admin who pressed “Start”

Audio capture begins immediately

System begins streaming real-time text to:

Original transcript buffer

Language translation buffers (on demand per user language selection)

User Experience:
Users immediately begin receiving text in the selected language

If a user arrives late, they receive the full transcript so far

Admin Experience:
Simple Admin View shows large buttons:
Pause | Stop | (Disabled: Start) | Restart (disabled)

Full Admin View shows all session parameters

26.3 Pause
Conditions:
Only controlling admin device can pause

Session must be active

No other admin may interrupt

If another admin requests control:

10-second delay

Auto-transfer unless controlling admin denies

Effects:
Audio input stops being processed

Translation generation pauses

Transcript buffers close temporarily (no new text appended)

System enters sessionPaused = true

User Experience:
Users see:
“Translation paused…”
(or admin-customized message)

User interface does not require any taps

Users remain at the Live Updating section

Admin Experience:
Buttons become:
Resume | Stop | Restart (disabled)

26.4 Resume
Conditions:
Only controlling admin device can resume

Session must be paused

No other admin interruption allowed except via approved control transfer

Effects:
Audio capture resumes

Original text transcript resumes

All active translations resume

System returns to sessionPaused = false

User Experience:
Live translation resumes automatically

Any user who scrolled upward:

Remains where they scrolled

Auto-returns to Live Updating section after 60 seconds of no interaction

26.5 Stop
Conditions:
Only controlling admin device may stop

Session must be active or paused

No other admin may override without control transfer

Effects:
Audio capture stops

All translation pipelines flush

Transcript buffers finalize

System enters sessionActive = false

System finalizes:

Original transcript

All language transcripts used during the session

Final text generated, banner added (not included in saved transcript files)

3-minute user-access window begins

User Experience:
Users see the final transcript

Banner appears at the bottom

After 3 minutes:

Screen automatically clears to the default idle view

Admin Experience:
Buttons become:
Start | Restart | (Pause/Resume disabled)

Admin can download transcripts

26.6 Restart
Conditions:
Session must be fully stopped

Any admin may press Restart

Restart button is disabled during active or paused sessions

The Meaning of Restart:
Restart = Start a new session within the same room.

Effects:
New session ID created

All buffers cleared

New transcript begins at zero

Users instantly begin receiving text from the new session

User Experience:
Users do not need to do anything

If they remained on the page:

Transcript from previous session disappears

New live translation begins automatically

26.7 Session Timeout Rules
Admin Timeout (Global Inactivity Period)
If controlling admin leaves or is inactive for admin-configured timeout (default: 3 hours):

Control is lost

Session ends gracefully

Transcript finalizes

Users continue to see transcript for 3 minutes

User Timeout (Transcript retention)
Users may scroll and remain on the page indefinitely

After 60 seconds of no interaction when scrolled away:

Their view automatically returns to the Live Updating section

No effect on the session itself

No user action can end a session

26.8 Control Transfer Logic
This logic applies during any part of the session lifecycle:

Non-controlling admin presses a control button

System prompts controlling admin:

“Admin X requests control. Deny?”

10-second countdown begins

If controlling admin takes no action → control transfers

If controlling admin presses Deny → requester is refused control

Control transfer is logged in system history

This ensures:

Predictability

A single controlling admin

No accidental session disruptions

26.9 Session Failure States
Audio failure
System retries automatically every 5 seconds

If no success → fallback to next device (see Room Microphone Priority rules)

Up to 3 cycles

After that:

Only admins receive alert

Users see nothing unusual

Session remains active but silent

Admins may manually fix the audio and press Resume/Start as appropriate

Network failure for controlling admin
If connection lost:

10-second grace period

If connection not restored:

Control becomes available

Other admin may request control

System crash scenario
On recovery:

Session state is restored from roomState

Transcript buffers restored

Users rejoin instantly

Admins must explicitly resume if audio was disrupted

26.10 Session Summary
Action	Who Can Trigger?	Allowed When?	Effects
Start	Controlling admin (first to press)	Inactive session	Begins translation
Pause	Controlling admin	Active session	Temporarily stops translation
Resume	Controlling admin	Paused	Resumes translation
Stop	Controlling admin	Active/Paused	Finalizes transcript
Restart	Any admin	Stopped only	Starts new session

CHUNK 27 — AUDIO & MICROPHONE INPUT SYSTEM (FULL DETAIL)
(Fully consolidated, complete, detailed, and consistent with every prior decision)

This section defines exactly how audio enters the system, how devices are selected, and how fallback works, following your strong requirement for simplicity, predictability, and low administrative burden.

27.1 Core Philosophy of the Audio System
The entire system is designed for maximum simplicity:

Only one audio source is used at a time per room.

Audio always arrives through the controlling admin’s device, unless explicitly configured otherwise.

Most setups will use one microphone plugged into:

A smartphone

A laptop

A USB audio interface

A mixing board output

Your system should work out-of-the-box with no specialized hardware knowledge and minimal configuration.

27.2 Audio Source Hierarchy (Simplified)
Every room has one audio source configuration active at any time:

Default Hierarchy (simplest case)
Admin device microphone input
(Usually: phone mic, laptop mic, or line-in from soundboard)

Optional room-designated external device
(e.g., a dedicated translation laptop, if configured)

Admin can configure a custom priority list per room:
A list of possible device sources (e.g., Admin Phone A, Laptop B, iPad C)

Ordered from highest to lowest priority

System tries them in order

But these are only device-level sources, never per-device internal inputs.
No complicated interface selection, no channel mixing.

27.3 Audio Source Configuration (Admin Panel)
The Admin Panel includes a section:

Room → Audio Source Priority
Admins can:

See available admin devices currently connected to the room’s admin interface

Add or remove devices from the room’s audio priority list

Reorder the list via drag-and-drop

Set one device as the default source

Examples:

“Sanremo Main Session – Audio Sources”

John’s iPhone (default)

Back Booth Laptop

Pastor’s Tablet

This is the only audio configuration the admin ever needs.
No extra technical complexity.

27.4 How the System Chooses the Audio Source
During Session Start:
When the controlling admin presses Start, the system:

Looks at the room’s priority list

Chooses the first device from the list that is online

Uses that device’s audio input

If a device in the priority list connects after session start:
No change occurs automatically

The session continues using its existing audio source

Admin may choose to Restart the session to switch

If controlling admin changes (via control transfer):
Audio source does not change

Audio source remains tied to the room’s assigned current device

27.5 Audio Flow Architecture
Device → Browser → Streaming Encoder → Speech-to-Text → Translation → User
The browser captures audio at low latency

Audio is streamed to the processing server

Speech-to-text converts it into the Original Transcript

Text is then routed through translation engines to create:

English

Italian

Spanish

Etc. (all languages selected by users)

Users receive lines via WebSocket events

27.6 Audio Failure Handling (Simple but Robust)
Failure Condition Examples
Microphone unplugged

Device permission revoked

Browser frozen

Device goes offline

Audio input freezes or is silent for > X seconds

Failure Handling Sequence
System detects failure

Automatic retry for 5 seconds

If still failing:

Switch to next device in room priority list

Retry the entire list up to 2 cycles

If no device works:

Users see nothing unusual

Admins receive a silent alert:

“Audio input lost. Attempting to reconnect.”

Session remains active

Translation is paused automatically

Admin must fix the issue and press Resume

Why Users See Nothing
Your requirement:

“Everything should be as transparent and simple as possible for users.”

So:

No popup

No warning

No disruption

They simply stop receiving text until translation resumes

27.7 Manual Switching of Audio Source
Admins may manually switch sources by:

Stopping the session

Restarting the session

Manual switching is deliberately not allowed during an active session, to avoid:

Latency spikes

Audio glitches

Transcript fragmentation

Restarting ensures:

Clean translation

Consistent audio

Predictable user experience

To keep everything simple:

CHUNK 30 — ADMIN SESSION STATE MACHINE (FULL LOGIC)
(Complete, consolidated, precise, and aligned with every rule established so far.)

This section defines the exact internal logic that determines how a session behaves under every admin action, system condition, microphone failure, control handoff, and timeout scenario.

This is the “brain” of the session.

30.1 Core Principles of the Session State Machine
The state machine is built around a few absolute, non-negotiable rules:

1. Only one admin device controls Start/Stop/Pause/Resume at a time.
Control is exclusive, transferable, and cannot be bypassed.

2. Users never interact with the session logic.
Users simply receive translated text.

3. A room can have only one active session at a time.
Multiple rooms can run simultaneously; one session per room.

4. The session state must be predictable, simple, and recoverable.
5. Microphone failures do not end sessions.
Auto-recovery cycles handle these.

6. All timeouts are unified and admin-adjustable.
30.2 Session States (Canonical List)
A session in any room must always be in exactly one of these six states:

1. IDLE
No audio listening

No translation

No transcript accumulating

Restart button available

Session has not begun or has fully ended and cleared

2. STARTING
Admin has pressed START

Microphone is initialized

Translation pipeline warmed up

Typically lasts <1 second

Automatically transitions to RUNNING

3. RUNNING
Audio captured

Real-time translation occurring

Transcript being delivered to users

Auto-scroll active for users

Pause/Stop allowed

4. PAUSED
Admin pressed PAUSE

Audio capture suspended

Users see “Translation paused…” banner

Transcript frozen

Resume allowed

Stop allowed

Restart NOT allowed

5. STOPPING
Admin pressed STOP

Translation pipeline shutting down

Transcript sealed

Users see “The translation has ended.” banner

Session moves to ended state

After 3 minutes, transcript clears for users

Auto-transition to IDLE

Restart becomes available

6. ERROR RECOVERY
Microphone failed

System auto-attempting recovery

Users remain unaware

If success → return to previous state

If failure after cycles → WARN ADMIN but stay in current state

30.3 Transition Diagram (Human-Friendly)
IDLE 
  -> START (admin) 
      -> STARTING 
          -> RUNNING

RUNNING 
  -> PAUSE (admin)
      -> PAUSED

RUNNING 
  -> STOP (admin)
      -> STOPPING 
          -> IDLE

PAUSED 
  -> RESUME (admin)
      -> RUNNING

PAUSED
  -> STOP (admin)
      -> STOPPING
          -> IDLE

RUNNING or PAUSED 
  -> MIC FAILURE 
      -> ERROR RECOVERY 
           -> RUNNING or PAUSED

IDLE
  -> RESTART (admin)
      -> IDLE (fresh transcript)
30.4 Control Ownership State Machine
Control of the session is separate from the session itself.

Control States
Owned

1 admin currently owns control

Requested

Another admin has requested control

Current owner has 10 seconds to deny

Transferred

Ownership moved to the requesting admin after timeout

Released

Current owner voluntarily releases control

Lost due to inactivity

After admin timeout (default 2.5 hours)

Session ends

Control resets to “unclaimed”

30.5 Full Logic of Control Requests
Admin B requests control while Admin A has control
System sends:

“Admin B is requesting control — deny?”

Admin A has 10 seconds:

If A presses DENY → A keeps control

If A does nothing → B gets control

This rule is universal and always applied.

If multiple admins request control
Only the first request is processed.
Others are ignored for 10 seconds until resolved.

If the controlling admin disconnects temporarily
They retain control unless:

They fail to return within the admin inactivity timeout (2.5 hours default)

Another admin requests control and gains it through the same rules

30.6 STOP vs. RESTART Logic
STOP
Ends translation

Ends session

Triggers transcript finalization

Shows end banner to users

Users see transcript for 3 minutes

After 3 minutes → user screen clears

Admin sees session in IDLE state

Restart button appears

RESTART
Only available in IDLE

Clears old transcript

Does not start session

Keeps control with current admin

Prepares clean slate

30.7 Microphone Failure Logic
Microphone failures move the session into ERROR RECOVERY state without stopping the session.

Users NEVER see errors.

Recovery Sequence
If mic fails:

Wait 5 seconds → auto retry

If still bad → switch to next device in priority list

If all devices fail → repeat full cycle 2 more times

If still failing after all cycles:

Session continues

Admin gets WARNING

Users see nothing

Admin may manually STOP or attempt hardware fix

System keeps retrying every 10 seconds indefinitely

Session never ends automatically due to audio failure.

30.8 Unified Timeouts
User inactivity timeout (60 seconds)
Only affects scrolling

No effect on session state

User transcript visibility timeout (3 minutes after STOP)
Transcript disappears after 3 minutes

Session is fully ended on user side

Admin inactivity timeout (default 2.5 hours, adjustable)
Applies only to controlling admin

If exceeded while session is RUNNING or PAUSED:

Session auto-STOPS

Transcript saved

Session goes to IDLE

Control resets

Session timeout (global 3 hours, adjustable)
If the browser tab is inactive for 3 hours

Session autostops

Same as above

Both timeouts are unified and simple.

30.9 Multi-Room Session State Independence
Each room maintains:

Its own session state

Its own control owner

Its own microphone list

Its own transcript

Its own URL

Its own QR code

No cross-room interference.

All user and admin rules apply identically to each room.

30.10 Persistence of Session Metadata
For each active session:

Current state

Transcript buffer (rolling last hour)

Control owner

Room configuration

Microphone priority list

Bible version mapping

User language selections (per device cookie)

Admin inactivity timers

Session start timestamp

All persist server-side.

30.11 Entire State Machine Summary Table
Event	From State	To State	Notes
Admin presses START	IDLE	STARTING → RUNNING	Start pipeline
Admin presses PAUSE	RUNNING	PAUSED	Users see banner
Admin presses RESUME	PAUSED	RUNNING	Resume pipeline
Admin presses STOP	RUNNING/PAUSED	STOPPING → IDLE	Ends session
Admin presses RESTART	IDLE	IDLE	Clears transcript
Mic failure	RUNNING/PAUSED	ERROR RECOVERY	Auto retry + fallback
Recovery success	ERROR RECOVERY	Previous	Users unaffected
Control request	Any	Same	With deny option

CHUNK 33 — SYSTEM INFRASTRUCTURE, HOSTING & DEPLOYMENT (FULL DETAIL)
This chunk covers the production architecture, hosting options, deployment model, scaling, storage, security considerations, costs tradeoffs, backup/monitoring, and operational runbook. It’s written so your dev team can implement the system with minimal re-interpretation.

33.0 High-level objectives for infrastructure
Low-latency, real-time text delivery (WebSocket or Server-Sent Events).

Very low bandwidth for listeners (text only).

Simple, mobile-first admin and user apps served reliably.

Durable transcript storage (TXT/PDF) with 60-day retention.

Small hosting cost target — prefer free/low-cost tiers for dev/early production.

Easily deployable and maintainable CI/CD pipeline.

Privacy & security: HTTPS everywhere, minimal PII, secure admin auth.

Monitoring and graceful degradation: translate failures and audio failures should be admin-notified but user-transparent.

33.1 Recommended overall architecture (logical)
Edge CDN / Static hosting for the front-end web app (HTML/CSS/JS), fast global delivery.

Application server(s) for:

WebSocket / SSE endpoints that push translated lines.

Admin APIs, room/session state machine, control arbitration.

Transcript file generation (TXT/PDF).

STT + Translation layer:

Real-time STT (speech → text) streaming service. Could be a managed API or a self-hosted model if you run GPUs.

Translation engine (cloud API or local model).

Persistent storage:

Object storage (S3-compatible) for saved transcript files (TXT/PDF).

Relational DB (Postgres) or managed alternative for metadata (rooms, sessions, admins, mic lists, retention policies).

Message queue / stream (optional but recommended) — light queue (Redis streams / Kafka / RabbitMQ) to decouple STT, translation, and delivery.

Monitoring & logging — centralized logs, metrics, and alerting.

CI/CD — GitHub Actions / GitLab CI / similar to build, test, and deploy.

33.2 Component choices & tradeoffs (practical recommendations)
Frontend (user + admin apps)
Framework: React (or lightweight Svelte/Vue) — mobile-first responsive. Use Tailwind for quick styling.

Hosting: Vercel / Netlify / Cloudflare Pages for static assets and SSR if desired.

Why: free/low-tier, global CDN, simple CI/CD integration.

Note: free tiers have limits—sufficient for small churches but test under load.

App server (real-time + API)
Languages: Node.js/TypeScript, Deno, or Python (FastAPI). Node has widest WebSocket eco.

Servers:

Prefer containerized services (Docker) deployed to:

Cloud Run (GCP), AWS Fargate, DigitalOcean App Platform, Fly.io, or Render.

Alternatively, Vercel supports serverless functions but long-lived WebSockets are easier on Cloud Run / Fly.io / dedicated servers.

Real-time:

Use WebSocket for two-way admin control / low latency text push.

Use Redis (pub/sub) or managed message broker to broadcast messages across multiple app server instances.

STT + Translation
Options:

Managed APIs (fastest to implement): Google Cloud Speech-to-Text + Google Translate, Azure Speech + Translator, AWS Transcribe + Translate, OpenAI endpoints where available — depending on desired accuracy/pricing.

Hosted models (self-hosted): Vosk/Whisper (STT) + Open-source translation models (Marian, M2M, etc.) on GPU instances — lower per-run cost but higher ops overhead.

Recommendation: Start with managed STT+translation APIs to iterate quickly; evaluate on accuracy and cost. Later, evaluate hybrid/self-hosting for predictable monthly cost if usage grows.

Database & Storage
Relational DB: PostgreSQL (managed: Supabase, AWS RDS, Neon, PlanetScale for MySQL) for rooms, admins, sessions, mic lists, user prefs.

Object Storage: S3 or S3-compatible (DigitalOcean Spaces) for transcript files (TXT/PDF). Keep files versioned and use lifecycle rules to auto-delete after 60 days.

Caching / Streams: Redis for ephemeral session data, fast pub/sub, and small queues.

File generation (TXT/PDF/DOCX)
Use server-side PDF generation (headless Chromium printing of a text template, or report libraries) and a docx library if docx required.

Save generated files to object storage and expose admin-only download links (signed, time-limited).

33.3 Deployment & scaling model
Scale vertically/horizontally for app servers: use autoscaling (Cloud Run, Fargate) based on CPU, memory, and WebSocket connections.

WebSockets: require sticky sessions or distributed pub/sub (Redis) — prefer Redis pub/sub + multiple instances behind a load balancer.

STT/Translation: scale separately; these are often the cost drivers. Consider pooling translation requests and batching small phrases.

Storage: object storage scales seamlessly.

DB: choose managed DB with automated backups and failover.

33.4 Networking, domain, and persistent URL / QR code considerations
Persistent URL: each room uses a stable URL (/r/<roomSlug>). QR code encodes that URL. Store the QR as an asset (SVG/PNG) in object storage and serve on admin panel.

HTTPS everywhere: enforce HTTPS with HSTS. Use automatic certificate providers (Let’s Encrypt or platform-managed).

CORS: carefully allow only your frontend origins for admin APIs; public room pages are public.

33.5 Authentication & security
Admin auth: email + password, hashed with Argon2/Bcrypt, issue short-lived JWTs or secure server session cookies (SameSite, Secure).

Admin actions protected by JWT and scope checks; audit log all admin actions (start/stop/control transfers).

User pages: no auth; users get ephemeral connections; no PII stored unless explicitly collected.

Data minimization: avoid storing personal data about listeners. Use anonymous device hashes/cookies responsibly.

Transcript access: admin-only downloads; links should be signed (time-limited).

Encryption: at-rest encryption for DB & object storage if supported.

33.6 Backup, retention & lifecycle
Transcripts: saved to object storage and retained for 60 days, then garbage-collected by lifecycle rules.

DB backups: scheduled automatic backups daily with at least 14-day retention (longer as budget permits).

Disaster recovery: document RTO/RPO targets and test restoration procedures.

33.7 Monitoring, logging & alerts
Metrics to capture:

Active WebSocket connections per room

STT latency and error rate

Translation latency and error rate

Transcript generation times

Disk and object storage usage

Tools: Prometheus/Grafana, or managed alternatives (Datadog, New Relic). Use Sentry for error tracking.

Alerts: notify admins (email/SMS/push) when STT or translation fails for more than configurable threshold, when object storage near quota, or when DB is unhealthy.

Audit logs: store admin actions (who started/stopped/edited) for compliance.

33.8 Cost considerations & hosting suggestions
Minimum viable (lowest cost):

Frontend: Vercel/Netlify/Cloudflare Pages (free/cheap).

App server: small managed instance on Render / Fly.io / Cloud Run (pay-as-you-go).

DB: free tier Postgres (Heroku, Supabase free), but be cautious about connection limits.

STT/Translation: managed APIs — will be the largest ongoing cost.

Storage: DigitalOcean Spaces or S3 with lifecycle rules.

Scaling:

If usage grows, move to higher tiers or switch STT/MT to a plan with volume discounts or self-hosted models.

Estimate: impossible to give exact numbers without expected minutes/hour, languages per session, and concurrent users. (If you want, give me expected weekly minutes and number of languages and I’ll produce a cost estimate.)

33.9 Operational runbook (how to bring this live)
Provision domain and CDN (Vercel / Netlify / Cloudflare) and verify HTTPS.

Provision DB and object storage (Postgres + S3).

Build frontend and deploy to static host.

Deploy app servers (Cloud Run/Fly/Render) with Redis and DB connections.

Integrate STT + translation APIs and implement local fallback handling.

Set up CI/CD (GitHub Actions to deploy on push to main).

Create admin account, create first room, generate QR.

Test end-to-end with short sample audio and multi-language clients.

Enable monitoring & alerts.

Go live in pilot mode (one church, limited usage) and iterate.

33.10 PDF/TXT/DOCX file generation & download strategy
Generate server-side on session STOP (or on-demand when admin requests).

TXT: stream simple plain UTF-8 text file; fast and tiny.

PDF: render an HTML template (with chosen font, line spacing) and convert to PDF with headless Chromium (puppeteer) or a server library. Store in object storage.

DOCX: optional; use a docx generation library server-side.

File naming: YYYYMMDD_roomSlug_language_v2.3.txt/pdf/docx (include spec version in filename as you requested).

Downloads: admin-only signed URLs that expire after short time (e.g., 1 hour).

33.11 Reliability & fallback best practices
Use Redis pub/sub so multiple app instances can coordinate and broadcast lines.

For WebSockets, use a managed solution if possible (e.g., Cloud Run + Redis) or specialized providers for scale.

Have health-check endpoints so orchestrator restarts failed instances quickly.

Gracefully degrade: if translation API is down, still record original transcript and notify admins.

33.12 Data privacy & compliance
Keep transcripts for 60 days — document retention policy and give admins ability to delete transcripts earlier.

If you operate in jurisdictions with data regulations (GDPR, etc.), provide mechanisms to:

Delete user data (if you store any).

Provide data export for admins (they already can download transcripts).

Avoid recording PII from users; keep minimal logs.

33.13 Multi-room, multi-instance coordination
Room state should be authoritative in the DB and cached in Redis for low-latency reads.

All app servers subscribe to room channels for broadcasting events (control transfer, new line).

When an admin acts, the app server persists to DB and publishes to the room channel.

33.14 Initial MVP hosting recommendation (practical)
Frontend: Vercel or Netlify

App server & Real-time: Cloud Run or Fly.io (better WebSocket support)

DB: Supabase (managed Postgres) for faster startup

Redis: Upstash or managed Redis

Object storage: DigitalOcean Spaces or S3

STT/Translation: start with managed cloud APIs (Google/Azure/OpenAI depending on testing)

Monitoring: Sentry + Prometheus/Grafana or Datadog

This combo minimizes ops and cost while giving good performance for small-to-moderate scale.

CHUNK 34 — SECURITY, PRIVACY, COMPLIANCE & DATA-GOVERNANCE
This chunk consolidates all security-related decisions we've made across the entire project and adds fully detailed, non-redundant descriptions suitable for engineering, legal, and deployment use. No prior details are removed; all are merged coherently.

34.0 Guiding Principles
Your system has four overriding principles:

User Simplicity & Transparency
Users never log in, never manage accounts, never handle authentication. Everything must “just work.” No PII about users is stored.

Admin Security
Admin access uses email + password only. Admin actions always require authenticated sessions.

Strict Data Minimization
Only store what is absolutely required (session state, transcripts, admin accounts, room configurations).
No personal user identity, no user device ID beyond ephemeral cookies.

Compliance Without Complexity
Make the system compliant with common international standards (GDPR, CPRA/CCPA, and general security best practices) without imposing complexity on users or admins.

34.1 User Privacy Model
34.1.1 No User Accounts
Users never create accounts, usernames, or passwords.

A user can enter any room by visiting a simple URL or scanning a QR code.

Cookies are used only to store:

Selected language

Display preferences (font, line height, theme, high-contrast)

Possibly room preference cache

Cookies expire after 60 days of inactivity.

34.1.2 No Personally Identifiable Information (PII)
No email, no phone numbers, no names, no IP logs tied to individuals.

Only anonymous metrics may be logged (e.g., number of users in a room).

34.1.3 Cookies & Local Storage
Only anonymous preference data is stored.

Cookies marked as:

Secure

SameSite=Lax

Not storing any unique identifiers or cross-site tracking data.

34.2 Admin Privacy & Authentication
34.2.1 Admin Accounts
Admins log in using:

Email

Password

Password hashed with Argon2id (preferred) or bcrypt (minimum).

No MFA requirement initially, but system should be expandable later.

34.2.2 Admin Sessions
Authentication handled via secure HTTP-only cookies or short-lived JWT.

Session lifetime: ~12 hours (configurable)

Auto-expire early on suspicious activity.

34.2.3 Access Control
All admin-only endpoints require authentication.

Only the admin who currently holds session control can run:

Start

Stop

Pause

Resume

Any admin can request control; if not denied after ~10 seconds (admin-adjustable), control automatically transfers.

34.2.4 Admin Logging
Every admin action is logged:

Who did it

When

What room/session

What action (start, stop, rename room, change fallback order, etc.)

Logs stored for minimum 60 days (configurable).

34.3 Data Storage & Retention
34.3.1 Transcripts
Stored for 60 days (hard rule).

Stored per-language, per-room:

YYYYMMDD_room_language.txt

.pdf also generated

Banner (end-of-session message) not included in saved transcripts.

Transcript always includes:

Original language

Each translated language used during the session

No timestamps by default (admin can enable them).

34.3.2 Deletion Rules
Automatic deletion via object-storage lifecycle (S3/S3-compatible).

Admin can manually delete transcripts.

34.3.3 Database Storage Minimization
Database stores:

Admin accounts

Rooms & room configuration

Session metadata (start/end times, state, controlling admin)

Microphone-device fallback order per room

User preference statistics (anonymous only)
Does NOT store:

Any user identity

Full session transcript (only ephemeral in Redis)

34.4 Security Architecture
34.4.1 HTTPS Always
Enforced sitewide using HSTS, strong TLS configuration, and platform-managed certificates.

No HTTP fallback allowed.

34.4.2 Content Security Policy
CSP enforced:

Only allow static assets from main domain

Block inline scripts

Only allow connections to:

App server

WebSocket endpoint

STT/translation APIs (server-side only)

Disallow all cross-site embedding.

34.4.3 Rate Limiting
Throttle brute-force attempts on admin login.

Throttle abusive API requests or malformed WebSocket activity.

34.4.4 WebSocket Security
WebSockets require:

Anonymous token (user)

Auth token (admin)

Admin WebSocket traffic isolated from user WebSocket traffic.

34.5 Compliance Considerations
34.5.1 GDPR/International
Users are anonymous; therefore the system holds minimal responsibility for data subject rights.

Transcripts may include personal speech content, so treat transcript storage as “user-generated content.”

Provide admins the ability to delete transcripts immediately (data erasure equivalent).

34.5.2 CCPA/CPRA
No “selling of data”; no user-specific data other than ephemeral cookies.

Admin emails are business-use only.

34.5.3 Children's Online Privacy
Users are anonymous; system does not intentionally collect data from minors.

Admin accounts can only be created by verified staff.

34.6 Security of STT & Translation
34.6.1 API Keys
All STT/MT keys stored in server-side secret manager (no embedding in client code).

Rotate keys every 90 days (recommended).

34.6.2 Fallback & Resilience
If STT fails:

Retry within 5 seconds.

Attempt fallback microphone device (admin-defined order).

Notify admins (non-intrusive).

Users receive clean flow of text or silence—no error messages.

34.7 Logging & Monitoring
34.7.1 Logging
Admin action logs

System error logs

WebSocket connection lifecycle

Translation/STT latency
All logs exclude PII.

34.7.2 Monitoring
Monitor:

CPU, memory, connection count

STT/translation throughput & errors

File storage usage

34.7.3 Alerts
Notify admins when:

Audio input fails consistently

Translation/STT becomes unavailable

DB or storage approaches quota

Admin notifications should be non-obtrusive and never visible to users.

34.8 Security for Multi-Room / Multi-Session
Rooms isolated logically.

Admin control only applies within a room.

Transcript storage per room.

Microphone fallback lists per room.

No cross-room data exposure.

34.9 Exported Files Security
Download links must:

Be signed

Expire after 60 minutes

Only be accessible by admins

DOCX, TXT, PDF must embed no hidden metadata beyond what is necessary.

34.10 Disaster Recovery & Backup
Daily DB backups with 14-day retention.

Disaster recovery plan:

Objective: restore within 30 minutes (RTO)

Data loss objective: ≤24 hours (RPO), although transcripts are flushed continuously and typically much safer.

Transcript files stored on replicated object storage.

CHUNK 35 — MULTI-LANGUAGE HANDLING, LANGUAGE SELECTION, AND SCRIPTURE LINKING
This chunk consolidates all decisions we made about language selection, fallback behavior, YouVersion integration, Scripture hyperlinking, and live transcript multilingual flow. Everything is expressed in full detail with no redundancy.

35.0 Overview
The system supports many languages for both:

Input (STT: Speech-to-Text)

Output (MT: Machine Translation)

Users choose a preferred language and receive a continuous translation stream in that language. Admins can configure default languages per room, fallback languages, and version-mapping for Scripture references.

The system aims for simplicity, ultra-low user friction, and full automation wherever possible.

35.1 User Language Selection
35.1.1 Initial Language Selection Screen
Shown only on the first visit or if cookies expired.

Displayed centrally and prominently before any transcript appears.

Includes:

A curated list of Top Languages selected by admin.

An “Other Languages…” entry that opens an alphabetical full list.

Full list sorted alphabetically by language name.

Once selected, the system immediately loads the transcript (existing last hour or new when session begins).

35.1.2 Persistent Language Preference
Stored in cookie for 60 days from last visit (room-specific).

If user visits multiple rooms, language preference persists across all rooms.

If entering a new room where the selected language is available, it is automatically applied.

35.1.3 Changing Language During a Session
A “Language” link at top of the UI allows changing languages at any time.

When changed:

User is delivered the full transcript for the last hour, translated into the new language.

User is placed immediately into Live Updating mode.

Auto-scroll resumes according to normal rules.

35.2 Admin Language Configuration
35.2.1 Room Default Language
Each room has a default language defined by admin.

New rooms inherit the last-created room’s default language, but can be changed before use.

Default language determines:

Which transcript can be corrected/editable by admins.

Default starting language for new users who have no stored preference.

35.2.2 Language Availability per Room
Admin can enable or disable languages per room.

If a language is disabled mid-session:

Users currently using that language continue receiving translations.

New users cannot select that language.

The text remains available in transcript export files.

35.2.3 Scripture Version Mapping per Language
Admin settings include:

List of supported Bible versions per language (e.g., ESV for English, RVR1960 for Spanish).

Mappings dictate:

Which version hyperlinks point to in YouVersion.

Which version to use in in-app fallback scripture display (if YouVersion missing).

35.3 Live Multilingual Transcript Behavior
35.3.1 Real-Time Delivery
For each spoken segment:

Original text is produced.

Machine translation generates all user-selected languages.

Users receive translated segments in their chosen language.

35.3.2 Transcript Structure
Real transcript includes:

Original (unaltered)

Translated versions (per language)

Transcript never rewrites original content.

No timestamps unless admin has enabled them.

35.3.3 Mid-Session Join Behavior
Users joining mid-session receive:

The entire last hour of transcript in their language.

Then the live stream.

Users are automatically scrolled to the live section unless interacting manually.

35.4 Scripture Hyperlinking
35.4.1 Reference Detection
Scripture references (e.g., “John 3:16”) detected automatically via:

Regex

Normalization of common book abbreviations

Detection is language-independent.

35.4.2 Behavior When Hyperlinks Appear
If YouVersion app is installed on the device:

Hyperlinks open directly in YouVersion.

Version used is selected based on admin mapping for that language.

If YouVersion is NOT installed:

Hyperlinks still appear.

When tapped:

A modal appears:
“YouVersion is not installed. Would you like to download it?”

Options:

Open App Store (Android/iOS)

Close (X)

Modal auto-dismisses after 5 seconds.

35.4.3 Admin Option to Disable Hyperlinking Entirely
Admin can toggle hyperlinking per room.

If disabled:

Scripture references remain plain text.

No modal, no detection overhead.

35.5 Translation Engine Behavior
35.5.1 Translation Accuracy
System relies on:

A single STT engine for original text.

A single MT engine for translations.

Consistency across languages ensures:

Uniform sentence boundaries.

Reduced jitter.

Predictability.

35.5.2 Editing
Only the default language for the room may be edited by admins.

Edits apply instantly to the transcript.

No flag is displayed to users.

Original language is never editable.

35.6 User Interface Behavior Across Languages
35.6.1 Fonts
Available fonts:

Sans-serif (default)

Serif

Dyslexia-friendly font

All chosen fonts must support:

All Unicode blocks used by supported languages.

Dynamic fallback for rare scripts.

35.6.2 Themes and Accessibility
Default theme follows device theme automatically (light/dark/high-contrast).

User overrides are available in “Aa” formatting control.

35.6.3 Auto-Scroll & Interaction
Auto-scroll pauses if user interacts (scrolls up).

Auto-resumes after 60 seconds of no interaction.

When auto-resuming, a smooth scroll moves the view to the live location.

35.7 Room-Level Language Behavior
35.7.1 Room-Specific Language Rules
Rooms define:

Default language

Language availability list

Scripture version mapping

Microphone fallback priority

CHUNK 37 — SYSTEM RECOVERY, NETWORK RESILIENCY & FAILURE-MODE BEHAVIOR
This chunk defines every rule for how the system behaves during interruptions, network failures, browser suspensions, device sleep, and reconnection events—for both Users and Admins. All rules have been harmonized with every prior decision.

37.0 GUIDING PRINCIPLES
The system must:

✓ Be completely seamless for users
Users should never experience confusing messages, errors, or interruptions.
• No warnings
• No alerts
• No pop-ups

The system must simply continue working whenever possible.

✓ Provide targeted information to admins
Only admins get alerts when something has actually gone wrong.

✓ Recover automatically
The system always attempts to resume:

microphone input

transcription

translation

user connections

scroll position

✓ Never require re-joining or re-logging for users
Users do not have accounts.
If a cookie is missing → treat them as new users.

✓ Handle all failures according to one unified framework
This was a global simplification requirement.

37.1 USER-SIDE NETWORK RECOVERY
Users must experience the simplest possible behavior.
No error messages. No dialogs. No prompts.

37.1.1 If user’s device temporarily loses connection (< 1 hour)
Behavior:

App detects loss of transcript feed.

Transcript freezes silently.

A hidden internal timer starts.

As soon as reconnection occurs:

User receives all missed transcript lines (from the last 60 minutes).

User is returned instantly to the Live Updating Section unless:

They have scrolled up manually

They have interacted with the UI

The 60-second auto-resume rule still applies (if they are inactive).

37.1.2 If connection loss lasts > 1 hour
This matches global user recovery rules.

Behavior:

User receives the last 1 hour of transcript only.

Auto-scroll resumes immediately.

No notifications or alerts are shown.

37.1.3 If user closes browser or app and returns
This is equivalent to network loss.

They automatically:

get the last 1 hour of transcript

return to the session

skip all alert dialogs

seamlessly resume

37.1.4 If user changes rooms
Equivalent to starting fresh in a new session:

They see the new room’s transcript

They are treated as a new user in that room

Their saved settings (language, font, theme, etc.) persist

37.2 ADMIN-SIDE NETWORK RECOVERY
Admins behave differently because they must see system status.

Rules are consistent across simple and full admin views.

37.2.1 If admin loses connection (< 15 seconds)
System attempts reconnection silently.

37.2.2 If loss > 15 seconds
Admin receives a warning:

“Connection lost. Attempting to reconnect…”

Behavior:

Admin retains control for 10 more seconds.

If reconnection fails and another admin is present:

Control transfer logic applies:

Admin receives:
“Your connection is unstable. Control may transfer automatically unless another admin denies.”

If no other admin is present:

System continues attempting reconnection.

Session does not stop automatically.

37.2.3 If admin device sleeps
Behavior:

Admin is treated as disconnected.

Reconnections follow the above logic.

If no reconnection for the global Admin Inactivity Timeout (default: 3 hours):

Session ends automatically.

37.2.4 If admin closes tab
This is treated as leaving the session.

Effects:

They lose control (unless they reconnect during grace window).

They may re-enter and request control later.

37.3 MICROPHONE & AUDIO SOURCE RECOVERY
Microphone rules were simplified:

37.3.1 Single main microphone per room
The system expects one audio input device per room.

37.3.2 Optional fallback list of devices
Defined in Admin → Audio Settings.

If microphone #1 fails:

Retry after 5 seconds.

If still failed:

Switch to next device.

If entire list fails:

Start again from #1.

Retry entire list twice.

If still failed:

Admin gets alert.

Users see nothing.

37.3.3 Microphone Recovery Priority
Always follow admin’s list.

This is now a simple, predictable system:

One main mic

Optional fallbacks

Quiet for users

Informative for admins

37.4 TRANSLATION ENGINE RECOVERY
37.4.1 If engine pauses for < 5 seconds
Silent retry.

37.4.2 If engine unresponsive > 5 seconds
Admin sees:

“Translation engine delay detected—attempting reconnection.”

Users see:

Nothing. The transcript simply pauses.

37.4.3 If engine comes back online
Admin alert clears.

Users instantly continue receiving translated text.

37.4.4 If engine fails > 30 seconds
Admin sees:

“Translation unavailable. Attempting fallback.”

If fallback enabled (future audio mode) → switch.

Otherwise → session continues but transcript pauses.

Users:

See no banners or alerts.

Transcript resumes instantly once engine is restored.

37.5 BROWSER BACKGROUND MODE
37.5.1 User background behavior
When user switches apps:

Transcript freezes.

Upon return:

If < 1 hour → receive missed lines.

If > 1 hour → receive last hour only.

37.5.2 Admin background behavior
Admin switching apps is treated as potential disconnect.

Rules:

Admin loses control if away too long (>= 15 seconds during unstable network).

If connection is stable, admin keeps control.

37.6 SESSION TIMERS (GLOBAL & UNIFIED)
These apply everywhere unless overridden in Admin → Settings.

37.6.1 User Inactivity
Never ends the session.

37.6.2 Admin Inactivity
Default: 3 hours
Adjustable.

If exceeded:

Session stops automatically.

Transcript remains visible to users for 3 minutes.

37.6.3 Post-Session Transcript Visibility
Users can read transcript for 3 minutes after admin stops session.

37.6.4 Transcript Retention
Server keeps transcript files for 60 days.

Admin alerts only

Everything here is fully aligned with all earlier chunks.

CHUNK 39 — SYSTEM-WIDE ERROR HANDLING & RESILIENCY (FULL DETAIL)
This chunk integrates all previous decisions about error-handling, fallback behavior, simplicity for users, and administrative visibility. As always, everything is written to be fully consistent with the entire spec so far.

39.0 PRINCIPLES OF ERROR HANDLING
The entire system follows these guiding principles:

1. Users should never experience interruptions
Users should never see technical messages, warnings, microphone errors, translation errors, or anything that could cause confusion.
Users simply continue seeing text — or a momentary pause in updates with no explanation.

2. Admins should see essential technical information only
Admins are the only ones who receive functional alerts, and only when relevant.

3. The system must self-recover whenever possible
Auto-retry mechanisms must run silently and efficiently.

4. All recovery attempts must minimize user and admin effort
Everything should “just work,” requiring almost no technical knowledge.

5. All failure states must fail safe
If something breaks:

the system does not crash

the user UI remains stable

the admin UI gives instructions or options

39.1 CLASSIFICATIONS OF ERRORS
All errors fall into 4 categories:

1. Audio Input / Microphone Errors
Microphone disconnected

Device audio interface failure

Bluetooth mic drops

Hardware unplugged

Device permissions revoked

2. Network / Connectivity Errors
Poor Wi-Fi

Connection drops

Slow or unstable data

3. Rendering / Client Errors
Browser freezes

Mobile UI fails

Font loading failures

Theme or accessibility errors

4. Translation Pipeline Errors
Translation API delays

Translation API not responding

Partial translation

System timeout

39.2 USER-FACING BEHAVIOR FOR ERRORS
Users see NO error messages or warnings.

User experience rules (already decided but now fully consolidated):

1. UI never flashes an error
The screen never changes except:

text may temporarily stop updating

auto-scroll continues as appropriate

scroll freeze rules remain unchanged

2. No banners, pop-ups, or interruption messages for users
Users should not be aware of any technical issues.

3. Transcript should remain readable at all times
Even if audio stops flowing, the user transcript remains visible and stable.

4. When translation resumes, new text simply appears
No “catch-up” notice
No “reconnected” message
No timeline markers
No system messages

39.3 ADMIN-FACING BEHAVIOR FOR ERRORS
Admins receive essential, non-technical alerts.

Alerts follow these principles:

No jargon

Clear, plain language

Visible but not intrusive

Must never obstruct controls

Admin Alerts Include:
1. Microphone Disconnected
Shown only to admins, e.g.:

After 5 seconds:

Still reconnecting… fallback device will be attempted.

After fallback attempts (configured by admin):

Unable to restore audio. Please check your microphone device.

2. Translation Delay
After 5 seconds of no translation:

Translation unavailable — system retrying.

Admins still control the session normally.

3. Network Failure
When admin’s device loses internet:

Network connection lost — attempting to reconnect.

4. Session Expiration Warning (Admin Only)
3 hours of inactivity triggers session close (as previously decided).
Admins get:

This room has been inactive for 3 hours. Session closed.

39.4 AUTO-RECOVERY RULES (GLOBAL)
Audio / Microphone Recovery
System attempts auto-resume after 5 seconds

If fail → attempts fallback microphone (admin-defined per room)

If still fail → cycles entire priority list twice

If still fail → admin notified

but session remains active

user stream unaffected (they simply see no new text)

Translation Recovery
Retry translation request for up to 10 seconds

If still failing → retry every 5 seconds

Admin notified

Users see nothing unusual

Network Recovery
If user loses network:

system reconnects automatically

when reconnected:

user receives last hour of transcript

then jumps to live position

and resumes auto-scroll rules

No messages shown to user.

If admin loses network:

admin sees notice

admin controls unavailable until network restored

other admins may request control

Rendering / UI Recovery
If browser freezes or UI fails:

user refreshes

system loads last hour of transcript

resumes in correct place

no messages

39.5 LOGGING OF ERRORS
Errors must be logged server-side only:

Logged:
Timestamp

Room

Admin device (not user devices)

Type of error

Reconnection attempts

Microphone fallbacks used

Translation API response delay

Not logged:
User identity

User device data

IP addresses (unless required for security)

Logs stay for 60 days (same as transcript retention).

39.6 FAIL-SAFE SCENARIOS

System stays active

No disruption for users

If translation server goes offline
System retries regularly

System gracefully closes

System automatically restarts

Last known transcript state restored

Users reconnected automatically

CHUNK 43 — SESSION ERROR HANDLING & RESILIENCY
This section covers everything that can go wrong during a session—microphone failures, network drops, admin disconnects, STT/MT model interruptions—and exactly how the system must recover, always prioritizing:

Simplicity for users

Transparency of system behavior

Admin-only visibility of technical issues

Automatic recovery whenever possible

Guaranteed uninterrupted user experience

43.1 FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLES (FINAL)
1. Users should never see error messages.
Users must never be exposed to system failures.

Users must not see:

“Microphone not detected”

“Connection lost”

“Reconnecting…”

No interruptions

No weird behavior

No warnings

No technical language

3. Only admins see error notifications.
Admin notifications must be:

Clear

Minimal

Non-technical unless needed

Only shown in admin UI (never to users)

43.2 MICROPHONE FAILURE HANDLING
Microphone failures are the most likely issue during a live session.

The system must handle these EXACTLY as follows:

If the active microphone fails:
Wait 5 seconds
Attempt auto-resume with the same microphone.

If still failing after 5 seconds:
Move to the next microphone in the room’s microphone priority list.

This list is set by the admin.

It is per-room, persistent, and reorderable.

Usually it contains only one microphone device, but the system allows multiple.

If all microphones fail once:
Automatically restart the cycle:

Try all microphones again

Same order

Up to 2 full retries (as previously decided)

If still failing after 2 full retries:

Pause translation

Notify admins:
“Audio source unavailable. Attempting recovery…”

Continue retry cycle indefinitely until recovery succeeds.

Users only see:
“Translation paused…”

When the microphone recovers:
Translation resumes instantly

Users jump back to Live Updating (after 60 seconds idle)

No transcript gaps if recovery is <10s

If recovery takes longer, STT continues from the new audio input point (natural)

43.3 NETWORK INTERRUPTION HANDLING
Two separate cases:

A. Users lose network connection
Users remain on transcript screen

When their network returns, they re-sync automatically

They receive all transcript lines from the last hour (from server cache)

No login required

No “rejoin” step

No message shown beyond standard UI behavior

User experience stays uninterrupted.

B. Admin loses network connection
Admin disconnection triggers the Admin Inactivity / Control Loss Rule, which we defined earlier:

If controlling admin disconnects:

Their device enters “inactive state”

They have 10 seconds to reconnect or return to the session tab
(Admin-adjustable)

After 10 seconds:

Other admins see that control is available

Control may be requested by any other admin
After request:

Auto-granted after 10 seconds unless denied

If the original admin is still offline, they cannot deny
→ Control transfers

If no other admins are present:

Session continues running indefinitely
(unless global inactivity time kicks in)

Microphone continues streaming

Users unaffected

43.4 STT / MT ENGINE FAILURE HANDLING
Speech-to-text or translation engine failures are possible.

If STT engine fails temporarily:
System attempts auto-restart every 3 seconds

Users see only “Translation paused…”

Admin sees:
“Speech recognition interruption. Recovering…”

If MT engine fails temporarily:
STT continues buffering text

System queues untranslated text

System retries MT translation for up to 60 seconds

Once MT recovers:

All buffered text is processed

Users receive the previously missed lines

Users auto-scroll back to live section (after 60 seconds idle)

If MT is completely down:
Admin sees warning

System continues listening and saving original transcript

Translated languages resume when available

Users see simple paused banner

43.5 ADMIN ERROR NOTIFICATION SYSTEM
Admin receives short, clear banners:

Possible Admin Alerts
“Microphone disconnected — attempting recovery…”

“Audio source unavailable — cycling fallbacks…”

“Translation service interruption — recovering…”

“Speech recognition error — retrying…”

“Admin control lost — transferring to next admin…”

Admins can always ignore these and the system will continue trying to self-correct.

43.6 USER ERROR EXPERIENCE (FINAL)
Users see nothing except:

“Translation paused…” (during major issues)

Auto-resume when recovery succeeds

Transcript continuity preserved

No system messages, no warnings, no confusion

This matches all previous decisions:

“Users should never be burdened with technical issues.”

“User experience must remain simple.”
